MARGIN:0px"><b>Forward-Looking Statements</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Certain statements in this Report constitute &#147;forward-looking statements&#148; MARGIN:0px" align=justify><b>ITEM 1. <u>Business </u></b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="PADDING-RIGHT:48px; MARGIN:0px" align=justify><b>GENERAL and RECENT DEVELOPMENTS </b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Par Pharmaceutical Companies, Inc., incorporated in 1978 as Par Pharmaceutical, Inc., is a Delaware holding company that, principally through its wholly owned operating subsidiary, Par Pharmaceutical, Inc. (collectively referred to herein as &#147;we,&#148; &#147;our,&#148; or &#147;us&#148;), is in the business of developing, licensing, manufacturing, marketing and distributing generic and branded drugs in the United States. &nbsp;We operate primarily in the United States as two business segments: Par Pharmaceutical (or &#147;Par&#148;), our generic products division, and Strativa Pharmaceuticals (&#147;Strativa&#148;), our branded products division. &nbsp;See Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#150; Note 19 &#150; &#147;Segment Information&#148;. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Prescription pharmaceutical products are sold as either generic products or branded products. &nbsp;Since our inception, we have manufactured, licensed and distributed generic pharmaceutical products. &nbsp;On November 17, 2011, we completed our acquisition of Anchen Incorporated and its subsidiary Anchen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (collectively referred to as &#147;Anchen&#148;), a privately held generic pharmaceutical company, for $413 million. &nbsp;The Anchen assets acquired include six currently marketed generic products (which are included in the section labeled &#147;Product Information&#148; below), numerous in-process research and development products, which included a pipeline of 29 filed Abbreviated New Drug Applications (&#147;ANDAs&#148;), a workforce of approximately 200 employees and leased facilities with manufacturing capabilities and research and development capabilities. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, we also had pending a $37.6 million acquisition of Edict Pharmaceuticals Private Limited (&#147;Edict&#148;), a Chennai, India-based developer and manufacturer of generic pharmaceuticals. &nbsp;The Edict assets acquired include numerous in-process research and development products, which includes a pipeline of 11 filed ANDAs, a workforce of approximately 100 employees and a facility with manufacturing capabilities and research and development capabilities. &nbsp;The acquisition of Edict was completed on February17, 2012. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We created a branded products division in 2005. &nbsp;We shipped our first branded product in 2005 and named our branded products division Strativa in 2007. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">In 2005, we divested one of our subsidiaries, FineTech Laboratories, Ltd., to a former officer and director. &nbsp;As a result of the divestiture, the FineTech business is being reported in our financial statements as a discontinued operation for all periods presented, as applicable. </p> <p style="PADDING-RIGHT:0px; MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:37px">Our principal executive offices are located at 300 Tice Boulevard, Woodcliff Lake, NJ 07677, and our telephone number is (201)&nbsp;802-4000. &nbsp;Additional information concerning our company can be found on our website at <font style=COLOR:#0000ff><u>www.parpharm.com</u></font>, including our Corporate Governance Guidelines, charters for the Audit Committee, Compensation and <a name=OLE_LINK44>Management Development Committee, and Nominating - Corporate Governance Committee of our Board of Directors, and our Code of Ethics. &nbsp;Our Code of Ethics applies to all of our directors, officers, employees and representatives. &nbsp;Amendments to our Code of Ethics and any grant of a waiver from a provision of the Code requiring disclosure under applicable SEC rules will be disclosed on our website. &nbsp;Any of these materials may also be requested in print by writing to Par Pharmaceutical Companies, Inc., Attention: Barry J. Gilman, General Counsel and Secretary, at 300 Tice Boulevard, Woodcliff Lake, NJ 07677. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:5px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Our fiscal year ends on December 31 of each year presented. &nbsp;Our fiscal quarters ended on the Saturday closest to each calendar quarter end for all periods up to and including 2009. &nbsp;Beginning in 2010, our fiscal quarters end on each calendar quarter end (March 31st, June 30th, and September 30th). &nbsp;Our electronic filings with the SEC, including Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K and any amendments to these reports, are available on our website, free of charge, as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file or furnish them to the SEC. &nbsp;Information on our website is not, and should not be construed to be, part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. &nbsp;The SEC maintains an internet site at <font style=COLOR:#0000ff><u>www.sec.gov</u></font> that contains reports, proxy and information statements and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>3</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always; TEXT-INDENT:48px; FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman" align=justify><b>Par Pharmaceutical -</b><font style="FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman"><b> Generic Products Division</b></font></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Generic drugs are the pharmaceutical and therapeutic equivalents of brand name drugs and are usually marketed under their generic (chemical) names rather than by brand names. &nbsp;Typically, a generic drug may not be marketed until the expiration of applicable patent(s) on the corresponding brand name drug. &nbsp;Generic drugs must meet the same governmental standards as brand name drugs, but they are sold generally at prices below those of the corresponding brand name drugs. &nbsp;Generic drugs provide a cost-effective alternative for consumers, while maintaining the safety and effectiveness of the brand name drug.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Our generic product line as of December 31, 2011, comprised prescription drugs consisting of approximately 55 product names (molecules), each with an associated ANDA approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (&#147;FDA&#148;), and approximately 200 SKUs (packaging sizes). &nbsp;Products sold by our generic products division are manufactured principally in the solid oral dosage form (tablet, caplet and two-piece hard shell capsule). &nbsp;In addition, we market several oral suspension products and injectables. &nbsp;We manufacture some of our own products, and we have strategic alliances and relationships with several pharmaceutical and chemical companies that provide us with products for sale through various distribution, manufacturing, development and licensing agreements. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">In January 2012, we announced that the key strategy for our generic products division will continue to be to focus on intelligent product selection and entrepreneurial business development. &nbsp;Our internal research and development is intended to target high-value, &#147;first-to-file&#148; or &#147;first-to-market&#148; generic product opportunities. &nbsp;A &#147;first-to-file&#148; product opportunity refers to an ANDA containing a Paragraph IV patent challenge to the corresponding brand product, which offers the opportunity for 180&nbsp;days of generic marketing exclusivity if approved by the FDA and if we are successful in litigating the patent challenge. &nbsp;A &#147;first-to-market&#148; product opportunity refers to a product that is the first marketed generic equivalent of a brand product for reasons apart from statutory marketing exclusivity, such as the generic equivalent of a brand product that is difficult to formulate or manufacture. &nbsp;Externally, Par will continue to concentrate on acquiring assets and/or partnership arrangements with technology based companies that can deliver similar product opportunities. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, we had 72 ANDAs filed with 19 confirmed first-to-file and four potential first-to-market product opportunities, including the then-pending acquisition of Edict. &nbsp;Additionally, Par is committed to high product quality standards and allocates significant capital and resources to quality assurance, quality control and manufacturing excellence. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">A practice within the industry is the use of &#147;authorized generics.&#148; &nbsp;Brand drug companies do not face any regulatory barriers to introducing a generic version of their own brand drugs, and they often license this right to a subsidiary or a generic distributor. &nbsp;Authorized generics may be sold during (and after) the statutory exclusivity period granted to the developer of a generic equivalent to the brand product. &nbsp;In the past, we have marketed authorized generics, including metformin ER (Glucophage XR<font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><sup>&#210;</sup></font>) and glyburide &amp; metformin HCl (Glucovance<font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><sup>&#210;</sup></font>) licensed through Bristol-Myers Squibb Company, and fluticasone (Flonase<font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><sup>&#210;</sup></font>) and ranitidine HCl syrup (Zantac<font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><sup>&#210;</sup></font>) licensed from GlaxoSmithKline plc. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, we marketed metoprolol succinate ER (Toprol XL<font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><sup>&#210;</sup></font>), zafirlukast (Accolate<font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><sup>&#210;</sup></font>) and budesonide (Entocort<font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><sup>&#210;</sup></font>) licensed through AstraZeneca. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Par markets our products primarily to wholesalers, drug store chains, supermarket chains, mass merchandisers, distributors, mail order accounts, and government, principally through its internal staff. &nbsp;Par also promotes the sales efforts of wholesalers and drug distributors that sell our products to clinics, governmental agencies and other managed health care organizations. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:48px" align=justify><b>Strativa Pharmaceuticals &#150; Branded Products Division </b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Brand products usually benefit from patent protection, which greatly reduces competition and provides a significant amount of market exclusivity for the products. &nbsp;This exclusivity generally allows a brand product to remain profitable for a relatively longer period of time as compared to generic products. &nbsp;In addition, due to the public awareness of the brand name and resulting consumer and physician loyalty, brand products may remain profitable even after the cessation of their patent related market exclusivity. &nbsp;We believe that brand products generally have limited competition, longer product life cycles and longer-term profitability than generic products. &nbsp;Strativa&#146;s products are marketed by its sales force, which communicates the therapeutic, health and economic benefits of our products to healthcare providers and managed care organizations. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Since its creation in 2005, Strativa has focused on supportive care, and marketed two products as of December 31, 2011: &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Megace<sup>&#174; </sup>ES (megestrol acetate) oral suspension, Strativa&#146;s first brand product, is a NanoCrystal<sup>&#174;</sup> Dispersion indicated for the treatment of anorexia, cachexia or any unexplained significant weight loss in patients with a diagnosis of AIDS. &nbsp;Strativa promoted Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES and generated prescription growth from launch following FDA approval in 2005 through 2007. &nbsp;Net sales growth began to moderate in 2008 and net sales declined in 2009, 2010 and 2011, principally due to a more challenging reimbursement environment, which led to lower prescription levels. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> (cyanocobalamin, USP) Nasal Spray is a prescription vitamin B12 treatment indicated for maintenance of remission in certain pernicious anemia patients, as well as a supplement for a variety of B12 deficiencies. &nbsp;We acquired Nascobal<font style="FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman"><b><sup>&#174;</sup></b></font> from QOL Medical, LLC on March&nbsp;31, 2009. &nbsp;Nascobal<font style="FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman"><b><sup>&#174;</sup></b></font> reached all-time prescription highs in 2011, and we project peak year sales in a range from $40 million to $50 million in the future. &nbsp;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In December 2010, we terminated our agreement with Solvay Pharmaceuticals, Inc. that provided for our branded sales force to co-promote Solvay&#146;s brand product Androgel<sup>&#174;</sup>. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In January 2011, we completed a modest reorganization of the Strativa management team (eliminating approximately ten positions) and refined our sales and marketing plan for each of Strativa&#146;s currently marketed products as part of our on-going efforts to maximize the value and potential of our existing product portfolio. &nbsp;We announced that the President of Strativa Pharmaceuticals resigned and that effective January 31, 2011, Patrick G. LePore, the Chairman and CEO, assumed day-to-day oversight of Strativa on an interim basis. &nbsp;In November 2011, Paul V. Campanelli, Chief Operating Officer and President, Par Pharmaceutical assumed responsibility for Strativa. &nbsp;We have taken steps to further align the Strativa home office sales and marketing team with the objectives of our sales force and to leverage the relevant expertise and experience within our Par Pharmaceutical generics division. &nbsp;In conjunction with these events, we recalibrated our target sales for our currently marketed products. &nbsp;Further information regarding such forecasts can be found in our Form 8-K filed January 6, 2012. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px"><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>4</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px; LINE-HEIGHT:12pt">In June 2011, we announced our plan to resize Strativa as part of a strategic assessment. &nbsp;We reduced our Strativa workforce by approximately 90 people. &nbsp;The remaining Strativa sales force focus their marketing efforts on Megace<sup>&#174; </sup>ES and Nascobal<sup>&#174; </sup>Nasal Spray. &nbsp;In connection with these actions, we incurred expenses for severance and other employee-related costs. &nbsp;The intangible assets related to products that are no longer a priority for our remaining Strativa sales force were fully impaired by these actions. &nbsp;We also had non-cash inventory write downs for product and samples associated with the products that are no longer a priority for our remaining Strativa sales force. &nbsp;In July 2011, Strativa returned to MonoSol Rx the U.S. commercialization rights for Zuplenz<sup>&#174; </sup>as part of the resizing of Strativa. &nbsp;In September 2011, Strativa executed a termination agreement with BioAlliance Pharma SA. returning all Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> rights and obligations to BioAlliance. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">We currently anticipate that the near term growth of Strativa will be based largely on focusing on the sales and marketing efforts of our current brand products. &nbsp;In the longer term, we will continue to consider strategic product or business acquisitions or licensing arrangements to expand Strativa&#146;s brand product line. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:13px; *</p></td> <td width=16 style=MARGIN-TOP:0px valign=bottom> <p style="PADDING-RIGHT:0px; PADDING-LEFT:0px; PADDING-BOTTOM:0px; MARGIN:0px; PADDING-TOP:0px">&nbsp;</p></td> <td width=130 style=MARGIN-TOP:0px valign=bottom> <p style="PADDING-RIGHT:0px; PADDING-LEFT:0px; PADDING-BOTTOM:0px; MARGIN:0px; PADDING-TOP:0px">&nbsp;</p></td> <td width=130 style=MARGIN-TOP:0px valign=bottom> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>1</p></td></tr></table> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; FONT-SIZE:11pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px"><b>* </b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt>Manufactured by Par </font></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We seek to introduce new products through our research and development program, and through distribution and other agreements, including licensing of authorized generics and branded products, with pharmaceutical companies located in various parts of the world. &nbsp;As such, we have pursued and continue to pursue arrangements and relationships that share development costs, generate profits from jointly-developed products and expand distribution channels for new and existing products. &nbsp;Our more significant distribution and supply agreements are described in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#150; Note 11 &#150; &#147;Distribution and Supply Agreements.&#148; &nbsp;&nbsp;Our more significant research and development agreements are described in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#150; Note 10 &#150; &#147;Research and Development Agreements.&#148;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><b>RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:12px; FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman" align=justify><b>Par Pharmaceutical -</b><font style="FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman"><b> Generic Products Division</b></font></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Our research and development activities for generic products consist principally of (i) identifying and conducting patent and market research on brand name drugs for which patent protection has expired or is expected to expire in the near future, (ii) identifying and conducting patent and market research on brand name drugs for which we believe the patents are invalid or for which we believe we can develop a non-infringing formulation, (iii) researching and developing new product formulations based upon such drugs and (iv) introducing technology to improve production efficiency and enhance product quality. &nbsp;The scientific process of developing new products and obtaining FDA approval is complex, costly and time-consuming; there can be no assurance that any products will be developed regardless of the amount of time and money spent on research and development. &nbsp;The development of products may be curtailed at any stage of development due to the introduction of competing generic products or other reasons.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>6</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The research and development of our generic pharmaceutical products, including pre-formulation research, process and formulation development, required studies and FDA review and approval, has historically taken approximately two to three years to complete. Accordingly, we typically select products for development that we intend to market several years in the future. However, the length of time necessary to bring a product to market can vary significantly and depends on, among other things, the availability of funding, problems relating to formulation, safety or efficacy, and patent issues associated with the product.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We contract with outside laboratories to conduct biostudies, which, in the case of oral solids, generally are required in order to obtain FDA approval. &nbsp;These biostudies are used to demonstrate that the rate and extent of absorption of a generic drug are not significantly different from the corresponding brand name drug. &nbsp;Each biostudy can cost from approximately $0.2 million to $1.3 million. &nbsp;Biostudies are required to be conducted and documented in conformity with FDA standards (see &#147;Government Regulation&#148; below). &nbsp;During 2011, we spent approximately $10.3 million with outside laboratories to conduct biostudies for 26 potential new products. &nbsp;We intend to continue to contract for additional biostudies in the future. &nbsp;The FDA has also required Par to perform certain clinical studies. &nbsp;In 2011, we spent approximately $0.7 million related to these clinical studies, and we anticipate spending approximately $6 million in 2012. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">From time to time, we enter into product development and license agreements with various third parties with respect to the development or marketing of new products and technologies. &nbsp;Our more significant product development agreements are described in Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements &#150; Note 10 &#150; &#147;Research and Development Agreements.&#148; &nbsp;Pursuant to these agreements, we have advanced funds to several unaffiliated companies for products in various stages of development. &nbsp;As a result of our product development program, we or our strategic partners currently have approximately 72 ANDAs pending with the FDA.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:12px" align=justify><b>Strativa Pharmaceuticals &#150; Branded Products Division </b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The first step in obtaining FDA approval for a drug that has not been previously approved is pre-clinical testing. &nbsp;Pre-clinical tests are intended to provide a laboratory evaluation of the product to determine its chemistry, formulation and stability. &nbsp;Toxicology studies are also performed to assess the potential safety and efficacy of the product. &nbsp;The results of these studies are submitted to the FDA as part of an Investigational New Drug Application (&#147;IND&#148;). &nbsp;The toxicology studies are analyzed to ensure that clinical trials can safely proceed. &nbsp;There is a 30-day period in which the FDA can raise concerns regarding the trials proposed in an IND. &nbsp;If the FDA raises any concerns, the developer must address those concerns before the clinical trials can begin. &nbsp;An IND becomes effective after such 30&nbsp;day period if the FDA does not raise any concerns. &nbsp;Prior to the start of any clinical study, an independent institutional review board must review and approve such study.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">There are three main stages of clinical trial development:</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:84px; TEXT-INDENT:60px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:84px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">In Phase I, the drug is tested for safety, absorption, tolerance and metabolism in a small number of subjects. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:84px; TEXT-INDENT:60px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:84px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">In Phase II, after successful Phase I evaluations, the drug is tested for efficacy in a limited number of patients. &nbsp;The drug is further tested for safety, absorption, tolerance and metabolism. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:84px; TEXT-INDENT:60px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:84px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">In Phase III, after successful Phase II evaluations, further tests are done to determine safety and efficacy in a larger number of patients who are to represent the population in which the drug will eventually be used. </p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The developer then submits an NDA containing the results from the pre-clinical and clinical trials. &nbsp;The NDA drug development and approval process takes from approximately three to ten years or more. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Our current strategy for developing the Strativa portfolio is to bypass the substantial investments associated with the development of drugs through this process, and instead to focus on the profitability of our existing brand products (Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES and Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup>). &nbsp;In addition, we will consider opportunities to add to our portfolio of branded, single-source prescription drug products through in-licensing and the acquisition of late-stage development products or currently marketed products. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; LINE-HEIGHT:11pt"><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>MARKETING AND CUSTOMERS</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We market<b> </b>our generic products<font style=FONT-SIZE:9pt><b> </b></font>principally to wholesalers, drug store chains, supermarket chains, mass merchandisers, distributors, mail order accounts, and government, principally through our internal staff. &nbsp;Strativa&#146;s products are marketed by its sales force, which communicates the therapeutic, health and economic benefits of our branded products to healthcare providers and managed care organizations. &nbsp;Some of our wholesalers and distributors purchase products and warehouse those products for certain retail drug store chains, independent pharmacies and managed health care organizations.&nbsp; Customers in the managed health care market include health maintenance organizations, nursing homes, hospitals, clinics, pharmacy benefit management companies and mail order customers.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We have approximately 100 customers, some of which are part of larger buying groups.&nbsp; In 2011, our three largest customers in terms of net sales dollars accounted for approximately 53% of our total revenues, as follows: McKesson Drug Co. (21%), Cardinal Health, Inc. (20%), and AmerisourceBergen Corporation (12%). &nbsp;In 2010, our three largest customers in terms of net sales dollars accounted for approximately 51% of our total revenues, as follows: McKesson Drug Co. (20%), Cardinal Health, Inc. (16%), and AmerisourceBergen Corporation (15%). &nbsp;In 2009, our three largest customers in terms of net sales dollars accounted for approximately 45% of our total revenues, as follows: &nbsp;McKesson Drug Co. (16%), CVS Caremark (15%), and AmerisourceBergen Corporation (14%).&nbsp; We do not have written agreements that guarantee future business with any of these major customers, and the loss of any one or more of these customers or the substantial reduction in orders from any of such customers could have a material adverse effect on our operating results, prospects and financial condition.&nbsp; </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>7</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>ORDER BACKLOG</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The approximate dollar amount of open orders (gross sales basis), believed by management to be firm as of December 31, 2011, was approximately $36.6 million, as compared to approximately $7.1 million at December 31, 2010, and approximately $19.0 million at December 31, 2009. &nbsp;These orders represent unfilled orders as of December 31, 2011, along with orders that were scheduled to be shipped at December 31, 2011. &nbsp;Open orders are subject to cancellation without penalty. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p><a name=OLE_LINK20><a name=OLE_LINK23> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>COMPETITION</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The pharmaceutical industry is highly competitive. &nbsp;At times, we may not be able to differentiate our products from our competitors&#146; products, successfully develop or introduce new products that are less expensive than our competitors&#146; products, or offer purchasers payment and other commercial terms as favorable as those offered by our competitors. &nbsp;We believe that our principal generic competitors are Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, Sandoz Pharmaceuticals, Mylan Laboratories, and Watson Pharmaceuticals, based upon sales volumes. &nbsp;Our principal strategy in addressing our generic competition is to offer customers a consistent supply of a broad line of generic drugs at competitive pricing. &nbsp;There can be no assurance, however, that this strategy will enable us to compete successfully in the industry or that we will be able to develop and implement any new or additional viable strategies. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:37px">The Hatch-Waxman amendments to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act provide for a period of 180&nbsp;days of generic marketing exclusivity for each applicant that is first to file an ANDA containing a certification of invalidity, non-infringement or unenforceability related to a patent listed with respect to the corresponding brand drug (commonly referred to as a &#147;Paragraph&nbsp;IV certification&#148;). &nbsp;The holder of an approved ANDA containing a Paragraph&nbsp;IV certification that is successful in challenging the applicable brand drug patent(s) generally enjoys higher market share and revenues during this period of marketing exclusivity. &nbsp;At the expiration of the exclusivity period, other generic distributors may enter the market, resulting in a significant price decline for the drug. &nbsp;(In some instances, price declines have exceeded 90%.) &nbsp;As a result of price declines, we may at our discretion provide price adjustments to our customers for the difference between our new (lower) price and the price at which we previously sold the product then held in inventory by our customers. &nbsp;These types of price adjustments are commonly known as shelf stock adjustments. &nbsp;There are circumstances under which, as a matter of business strategy, we may decide not to provide price adjustments to certain customers, and consequently, we may lose future sales volume to competitors rather than reduce our pricing. </p> <p style="FONT-SIZE:6pt; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px" align=justify>&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Competition in the generic drug industry has also increased due to the advent of authorized generics. &nbsp;&#147;Authorized generics&#148; are generic pharmaceutical products that are introduced by brand companies, either directly or through partnering arrangements with other generic companies. &nbsp;Authorized generics are equivalent to the brand companies&#146; brand name drugs, but are sold at relatively lower prices than the brand name drugs. &nbsp;This is a significant source of competition for us, because brand companies do not face any regulatory barriers to introducing a generic version of their own brand name drugs. &nbsp;Further, authorized generics may be sold during any period of generic marketing exclusivity granted to a generic company, which significantly undercuts the profits that a generic company could otherwise receive as an exclusive marketer of a generic product. &nbsp;Such actions have the effect of reducing the potential market share and profitability of our generic products and may inhibit us from introducing generic products corresponding to certain brand name drugs. &nbsp;We have also marketed authorized generics in partnership with brand companies, including during the exclusivity periods of our generic competitors. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Increased price competition has also resulted from consolidation among wholesalers and retailers and the formation of large buying groups, which has caused reductions in sales prices and gross margin. &nbsp;This competitive environment has led to an increase in customer demand for downward price adjustments from the distributors of generic pharmaceutical products. &nbsp;Such price reductions are likely to continue, or even increase, which could have a material adverse effect on our revenues and gross margin.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The principal competitive factors in the generic pharmaceutical market include: (i) introduction of other generic drug manufacturers&#146; products in direct competition with our products, (ii) introduction of authorized generic products in direct competition with our products, particularly during exclusivity periods, (iii) consolidation among distribution outlets through mergers and acquisitions and the formation of buying groups, (iv) ability of generic competitors to quickly enter the market after the expiration of patents or exclusivity periods, diminishing the amount and duration of significant profits, (v) the willingness of generic drug customers, including wholesale and retail customers, to switch among pharmaceutical manufacturers, (vi) pricing pressures by competitors and customers, (vii) a company&#146;s reputation as a manufacturer and distributor of quality products, (viii) a company&#146;s level of service (including maintaining sufficient inventory levels for timely deliveries), (ix) product appearance and labeling, and (x) a company&#146;s breadth of product offerings. </p><a name=_DV_C49> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px"> Our brand products benefit from patent protection, making them subject to Paragraph IV patent challenges that could jeopardize our market exclusivity for these products. &nbsp;Consequently, competition<a name=_DV_M142> from generic equivalents, <a name=_DV_C51> and especially a successful Paragraph IV patent challenge against one of our brand products<a name=_DV_M143> , could have an adverse effect on Strativa. &nbsp;<a name=_DV_C53> In addition<a name=_DV_M144> , after patent protections expire, generic products can be sold in the market at a significantly lower cost than the <a name=_DV_C55> brand<a name=_DV_M145> version, and, where available, may be required or encouraged in preference to the <a name=_DV_C57> brand<a name=_DV_M146> version under third party reimbursement programs, or substituted by pharmacies for <a name=_DV_C59> brand<a name=_DV_M147> versions by law. &nbsp;<a name=_DV_C60> Strativa also faces competition from other brand drug companies. &nbsp;<a name=_DV_M148> Many of our brand competitors have longer operating histories and greater financial, research and development, marketing and other resources than we do. &nbsp;Consequently, many of our brand competitors may be able to develop products superior to our own. &nbsp;Furthermore, we may not be able to differentiate our products from those of our brand competitors or offer customers payment and other commercial terms as favorable as those offered by our brand competitors. &nbsp;The markets in which we compete and intend to compete are undergoing, and are expected to continue to undergo, rapid and significant change. &nbsp;We expect brand competition to intensify as technological advances and consolidations continue. &nbsp;</p></a><a name=_DV_M144> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px"><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>8</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <a name=_DV_M148> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p><a name=OLE_LINK30><a name=OLE_LINK32> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>RAW MATERIALS</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The raw materials essential to our manufacturing business are purchased primarily from U.S. distributors of bulk pharmaceutical chemicals manufactured by foreign companies.&nbsp; To date, we have experienced no significant difficulties in obtaining raw materials and expect that raw materials will generally continue to be available in the future.&nbsp; However, because the federal drug application process requires specification of raw material suppliers, if raw materials from a specified supplier were to become unavailable, FDA approval of a new supplier would be required. &nbsp;A delay of six months or more in the manufacture and marketing of the drug involved while a new supplier becomes qualified by the FDA and its manufacturing process is determined to meet FDA standards could, depending on the particular product, have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.&nbsp; Generally, we attempt to mitigate the potential effects of any such situation by providing for, where economically and otherwise feasible, two or more suppliers of raw materials for the drugs that we manufacture.&nbsp; In addition, we may attempt to enter into a contract with a raw material supplier in an effort to ensure adequate supply for our products.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><b>EMPLOYEES</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">At December 31, 2011, we had 819 employees. &nbsp;None of our employees are covered by any collective bargaining agreement. &nbsp;We consider our employee relations to be good. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>GOVERNMENT REGULATION </b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The development, manufacturing, sales, marketing and distribution of our products are subject to extensive governmental regulation by the U.S. federal government, principally the FDA, and, as applicable, the Drug Enforcement Administration, Federal Trade Commission (the &#147;FTC&#148;) and state and local governments. &nbsp;For both currently marketed and future products, failure to comply with applicable regulatory requirements can, among other things, result in suspension of regulatory approval and possible civil and criminal sanctions. &nbsp;Regulations, enforcement positions, statutes and legal interpretations applicable to the pharmaceutical industry are constantly evolving and are not always clear. &nbsp;Significant changes in regulations, enforcement positions, statutes and legal interpretations could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operation. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The enactment of current U.S. healthcare reform has a significant impact on our business. &nbsp;As examples, the current legislation includes measures that &nbsp;(i) significantly increase Medicaid rebates through both the expansion of the program and significant increases in rebates; (ii) substantially expand the Public Health System (340B) program to allow other entities to purchase prescription drugs at substantial discounts; (iii) extend the Medicaid rebate rate to a significant portion of Managed Medicaid enrollees; (iv) assess a 50% rebate on Medicaid Part D spending in the coverage gap for branded and authorized generic prescription drugs; and (v) levy a significant excise tax on the industry to fund the healthcare reform. &nbsp;&nbsp;The impacts of these provisions are included in our current financial statements. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Additionally, future healthcare legislation or other legislative proposals at the federal and state levels could bring about major changes in the affected health care systems, including statutory restrictions on the means that can be employed by branded and generic pharmaceutical companies to settle Paragraph IV patent litigations. &nbsp;We cannot predict the outcome of such initiatives, but such initiatives, if passed, could result in significant costs to us in terms of costs of compliance and penalties associated with failure to comply. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Controlled Substances Act and other federal statutes and regulations govern the development, testing, manufacture, safety, effectiveness, labeling, storage, record keeping, approval, advertising and promotion of our products. &nbsp;Non-compliance with applicable regulations can result in judicially and/or administratively imposed sanctions, including the initiation of product seizures, injunctions, fines and criminal prosecutions. &nbsp;Administrative enforcement measures may involve the recall of products, as well as the refusal of an applicable government authority to enter into supply contracts or to approve new drug applications. &nbsp;The FDA also has the authority to withdraw its approval of drugs in accordance with its regulatory due process procedures. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px"><b>New Drug Applications and Abbreviated New Drug Applications</b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">FDA approval is required before any new drug, including a generic equivalent of a previously approved brand name drug, may be marketed. &nbsp;To obtain FDA approval for a new drug, a prospective manufacturer must, among other things, as discussed below, demonstrate that its manufacturing facilities comply with the FDA&#146;s current Good Manufacturing Practices (&#147;cGMP&#148;) regulations. &nbsp;The FDA may inspect the manufacturer&#146;s facilities to ensure such compliance prior to approval or at any other time. &nbsp;The manufacturer is required to comply with cGMP regulations at all times during the manufacture and processing of drugs. &nbsp;To comply with the standards set forth in these regulations, we must continue to expend significant time, money and effort in the areas of production, quality control and quality assurance.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>9</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">In order to obtain FDA approval of a new drug, a manufacturer must demonstrate the drug&#146;s safety and effectiveness. &nbsp;There currently are two ways to satisfy the FDA&#146;s safety and effectiveness requirements:</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:54px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">1.</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:54px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px"><i>New Drug Applications (NDAs):</i> Unless the procedure discussed in paragraph 2 below is permitted under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, a prospective manufacturer must submit to the FDA an NDA containing complete pre-clinical and clinical safety and efficacy data or a right of reference to such data. &nbsp;The pre-clinical data must provide an adequate basis for evaluating the safety and scientific rationale for the initiation of clinical trials. &nbsp;Clinical trials are conducted in three sequential phases and may take up to several years to complete. &nbsp;At times, the phases may overlap. &nbsp;Data from pre-clinical testing and clinical trials is submitted to the FDA as an NDA for marketing approval.</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN:0px" align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:54px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">2.</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:54px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px"><i>Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs):</i> The Hatch-Waxman amendments to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act established a statutory procedure for submission, FDA review and approval of ANDAs for generic versions of brand name drugs previously approved by the FDA (such previously approved drugs are referred to as &#147;listed drugs&#148;). &nbsp;Because the safety and efficacy of listed drugs have already been established by the innovator company, the FDA waives the requirement for complete clinical trials. &nbsp;However, a generic manufacturer is typically required to conduct bioavailability/bioequivalence studies of its test product against the listed drug. &nbsp;The bioavailability/bioequivalence studies assess the rate and extent of absorption and concentration levels of a drug in the blood stream required to produce a therapeutic effect. &nbsp;Bioequivalence is established when the rate of absorption and concentration levels of a generic product are substantially equivalent to the listed drug. &nbsp;For some drugs (<i>e.g.,</i> topical anti-fungals), other means of demonstrating bioequivalence may be required by the FDA, especially where rate and/or extent of absorption are difficult or impossible to measure. &nbsp;In addition to the bioequivalence data, an ANDA must contain patent certifications, chemistry, manufacturing, labeling and stability data.</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN:0px" align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The Hatch-Waxman amendments also established certain statutory protections for listed drugs. &nbsp;Under the Hatch-Waxman amendments, approval of an ANDA for a generic drug may not be made effective for interstate marketing until all relevant patents for the listed drug have expired or been determined to be invalid or not infringed by the generic drug. &nbsp;Prior to enactment of the Hatch-Waxman amendments, the FDA did not consider the patent status of a previously approved drug. &nbsp;In addition, under the Hatch-Waxman amendments, statutory non-patent exclusivity periods are established following approval of certain listed drugs, where specific criteria are met by the drug. &nbsp;If exclusivity is applicable to a particular listed drug, the effective date of approval of ANDAs for the generic version of the listed drug is usually delayed until the expiration of the exclusivity period, which, for newly approved drugs, can be either three or five years. &nbsp;The Hatch-Waxman amendments also provide for extensions of up to five years for certain patents covering drugs to compensate the patent holder for the reduction in the effective market life of the patented drug resulting from the time spent in the federal regulatory review process.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">During 1995, patent terms for a number of listed drugs were extended when the Uruguay Round Agreements Act (the &#147;URAA&#148;) went into effect in order to implement the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (&#147;GATT&#148;) to which the United States became a treaty signatory in 1994. &nbsp;Under GATT, the term of patents was established as 20 years from the date of patent application. &nbsp;In the United States, the patent terms historically have been calculated at 17 years from the date of patent grant. &nbsp;The URAA provided that the term of issued patents be either the existing 17 years from the date of patent grant or 20 years from the date of application, whichever was longer. &nbsp;The effect generally was to extend the patent life of already issued patents, thus delaying FDA approvals of applications for generic products.</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px" align=justify>&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The Medicare Prescription Drug Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003 streamlined the generic drug approval process by limiting a drug company to only one 30-month stay of a generic drug&#146;s entry into the market for resolution of a patent challenge for ANDAs filed after August 18, 2003. &nbsp;This rule was designed to help maintain a balance between the innovator companies&#146; intellectual property rights and the desire to allow generic drugs to be brought to the market in a timely fashion. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The FDA issued a final rule on June 18, 2003 (the &#147;final rule&#148;), clarifying the types of patents that innovators must submit for listing and prohibiting the submission of patents claiming packaging, intermediates or metabolite innovations. &nbsp;Patents claiming a different polymorphic form of the active ingredient described in an NDA must be submitted if the NDA holder has test data demonstrating that the drug product containing the polymorph will perform in the same way as the drug product described in the NDA. &nbsp;These changes are consistent with concerns raised in 2002 by the FTC in its report on generic drugs. &nbsp;The final rule also clarifies the type of patent information that is required to be submitted and revises the declaration that NDA applicants must provide regarding their patents to help ensure that NDA applicants submit only appropriate patents. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>10</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The final rule was intended to make the patent submission and listing process more efficient, as well as to enhance the ANDA and 505(b)(2) application (described below) approval process. &nbsp;The changes were designed to enable consumers to save billions of dollars each year by making it easier for generic drug manufacturers to get safe and effective products on the market when the appropriate patent protection expires.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Section 505(b)(2) was added to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act by the Hatch-Waxman amendments. &nbsp;This provision permits the FDA to rely, for approval of an NDA, on data not developed by the applicant. &nbsp;A 505(b)(2) application must include identification of the listed drug for which the FDA has made a finding of safety and effectiveness and on which finding the applicant relies in seeking approval of its proposed drug product. &nbsp;A 505(b)(2) application may rely on studies published in scientific literature or an FDA finding of safety and/or efficacy for an approved product for support, in addition to clinical studies performed by the applicant. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The approval of a 505(b)(2) application may result in three years of exclusivity under the Hatch-Waxman amendments if one or more of the clinical studies (other than bioavailability/bioequivalence studies) were essential to the approval of the application and was conducted by the applicant. &nbsp;The approval of a 505(b)(2) application may result in five years of exclusivity if it is for a new chemical entity. &nbsp;If appropriate under U. S. patent laws, 505(b)(2) NDAs are eligible for the FDA&#146;s patent certification protection. &nbsp;Such approvals have the potential to be delayed due to patent and exclusivity rights that apply to the listed drug.<font style=FONT-SIZE:12pt> </font></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px"><b>Pricing Regulation</b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Successful commercialization of our products depends, in part, on the availability of governmental and third-party payor reimbursement for the cost of our products. &nbsp;Government authorities and third-party payors increasingly are challenging the price of medical products and services. &nbsp;On the government side, there is a heightened focus, at both the federal and state levels, on decreasing costs and reimbursement rates in Medicaid, Medicare and other government insurance programs. &nbsp;This has led to an increase in federal and state legislative initiatives related to drug prices, which could significantly influence the purchase of pharmaceutical products, resulting in lower prices and changes in product demand. &nbsp;With respect to the Medicaid program, certain proposed provisions of the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 went into effect January 1, 2007, and a final rule went into effect as of October 1, 2007, that resulted in changes to certain formulas used to calculate pharmacy reimbursement under Medicaid (currently under a stay of execution). &nbsp;If enacted, these changes could lead to reduced payments to pharmacies.&nbsp; Many states have also created preferred drug lists and include drugs on those lists only when the manufacturers agree to pay a supplemental rebate.&nbsp; If our current products or future drug candidates are not included on these preferred drug lists, physicians may not be inclined to prescribe them to their Medicaid patients, thereby diminishing the potential market for our products. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Moreover, government regulations regarding reporting and payment obligations are complex, and we are continually evaluating the methods we use to calculate and report the amounts owed with respect to Medicaid and other government pricing programs. &nbsp;Our calculations are subject to review and challenge by various government agencies and authorities, and it is possible that any such review could result either in material changes to the method used for calculating the amounts owed to such agency or the amounts themselves. &nbsp;Because the process for making these calculations, and our judgments supporting these calculations, involve subjective decisions, these calculations are subject to audit. &nbsp;In the event that a government authority challenges or finds ambiguity with regard to our report of payments, such authority may impose civil and/or criminal sanctions, which could have a material adverse effect on our business. &nbsp;From time to time we conduct routine reviews of our government pricing calculations. &nbsp;These reviews may have an impact on government price reporting and rebate calculations used to comply with various government regulations regarding reporting and payment obligations. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><b>Fraud and Abuse Regulation</b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Pharmaceutical companies are subject to various federal and state laws relating to sales and marketing practices intended to combat health care fraud and abuse. &nbsp;These include anti-kickback laws, false claims laws and FDA regulation of advertising and promotion of pharmaceutical products. &nbsp;We have incurred and will continue to incur costs to comply with these laws. &nbsp;While we intend to comply in all respects with fraud and abuse laws, there has been an increase in government enforcement efforts at both the federal and state level and, due to the breadth of regulation and the absence of guidance in some cases, it is possible that our practices might be challenged by government authorities. &nbsp;Violations of fraud and abuse laws may be punishable by civil and/or criminal sanctions including fines, civil monetary penalties, as well as the possibility of exclusion from federal health care programs. &nbsp;Any such violations could have a material adverse effect on our business. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px"><b>AWP Litigation</b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Many government and third-party payors reimburse the purchase of certain prescription drugs based on a drug&#146;s Average Wholesale Price or &#147;AWP.&#148; &nbsp;In the past several years, state and federal government agencies have conducted ongoing investigations of manufacturers&#146; reporting practices with respect to AWP, which they have suggested have led to excessive payments by state and federal government agencies for prescription drugs. &nbsp;We, as well as numerous other pharmaceutical companies, were named as a defendant in various state and federal court actions alleging improper or fraudulent practices related to the reporting of AWP and additional actions are anticipated. &nbsp;Refer to Item 3 &#150; &#147;Legal Proceedings&#148; and Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements <font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol>-</font> Note 17 &#150; &#147;Commitments, Contingencies and Other Matters&#148; for further information. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>11</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always"><b>Drug Pedigree Laws</b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">State and federal governments have proposed or passed various drug pedigree laws which can require the tracking of all transactions involving prescription drugs from the manufacturer to the pharmacy (or other dispensing) level. &nbsp;Companies are required to maintain records documenting the chain of custody of prescription drug products beginning with the purchase of such products from the manufacturer. &nbsp;Compliance with these pedigree laws requires implementation of extensive tracking systems as well as heightened documentation and coordination with customers and manufacturers. &nbsp;While we fully intend to comply with these laws, there is uncertainty about future changes in legislation and government enforcement of these laws. &nbsp;Failure to comply could result in fines or penalties, as well as loss of business that could have a material adverse effect on our financial results. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px"><b>Federal Regulation of Authorized Generic Arrangements</b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">As part of the Medicare Prescription Drug Improvement and Modernization Act of 2003, companies are required to file with the FTC and the Department of Justice certain types of agreements entered into between brand and generic pharmaceutical companies related to the manufacture, marketing and sale of generic versions of brand drugs. &nbsp;This requirement could affect the manner in which generic drug manufacturers resolve intellectual property litigation and other disputes with brand pharmaceutical companies, and could result generally in an increase in private-party litigation against pharmaceutical companies or additional investigations or proceedings by the FTC or other governmental authorities. &nbsp;Additionally, provisions in the Affordable Health Care for America Act H.R. 3962 that would limit Hatch-Waxman patent litigation settlements to generic drug entry dates and attorneys&#146; fees for the litigation parties (should it survive reconciliation with the pending Senate Bill, H.R. 3590) could also materially affect the ability for generic drug manufacturers to secure authorized generic agreements and resolve intellectual property litigation and other disputes with brand pharmaceutical companies generally.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px"><b>Other</b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In addition to the U.S. federal government, various states and localities have laws regulating the manufacture and distribution of pharmaceuticals, as well as regulations dealing with the substitution of generic drugs for brand name drugs. &nbsp;Our operations are also subject to regulation, licensing requirements and inspection by the states and localities in which our operations are located and/or in which we conduct business.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Certain of our activities are also subject to FTC enforcement actions. &nbsp;The FTC enforces a variety of antitrust and consumer protection laws designed to ensure that the nation&#146;s markets function competitively, are vigorous, efficient and free of undue restrictions. &nbsp;<font style="COLOR:#00007f; FONT-FAMILY:Arial">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">We also are governed by federal and state laws of general applicability, including laws regulating matters of environmental quality, working conditions, health and safety, and equal employment opportunity. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; Business Applications, Technology Operations, and Scientific Systems. &nbsp;Each department maintains its own development, implementation and support teams. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; </p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN:0px"><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><b>COMPANY STRENGTHS AND STRATEGIES</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Our goal is to successfully manage both our generic and branded businesses for the long term. &nbsp;We are striving to achieve sustainable long-term growth with enhanced profitability and improved cash flow. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:12px"><b>Par Pharmaceutical: &nbsp;Developing and Marketing Higher-Margin Generic Pharmaceuticals </b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Par Pharmaceutical, our generic products division, is committed to providing high-quality pharmaceuticals that are affordable and accessible to patients. &nbsp;<a name=OLE_LINK38><a name=OLE_LINK39>We ranked 5th in U.S. sales among all generic drug companies in 2011, according to IMS Health, and as of December 31, 2011 we manufactured, marketed or licensed generic prescription drugs consisting of approximately 55 product names (molecules), in the form of approximately 55 products (each with an associated ANDA), and approximately 200 SKUs (packaging sizes). &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Our generic pipeline included approximately 72 products awaiting FDA approval, which include 19 confirmed first-to-file and four potential first-to-market product opportunities as of December 31, 2011, including the then-pending acquisition of Edict. &nbsp;In recent years, we introduced generic versions of several major pharmaceutical products, including Toprol-XL<sup>&#174;</sup>, Entocort<sup>&#174;</sup>, Imitrex<sup>&#174;</sup>, Rythmol<sup>&#174;</sup>, Ultracet ER<sup>&#174;</sup> and Lotrel<sup>&#174;</sup>. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Par Pharmaceutical is focused on developing products with limited competition, significant barriers to entry and longer life cycles. &nbsp;Our success is also predicated on business development, including in-licensing, alliances and acquisitions, and cost efficiencies derived from global sourcing initiatives and operations. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:12px"><b>Strativa Pharmaceuticals: &nbsp;Building a Branded Pharmaceutical Business Focused on Specialty Markets </b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:24px">In 2005, we received approval for and introduced Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES, our first branded pharmaceutical product. &nbsp;On March 31, 2009, we acquired the rights to Nascobal<font style="FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman"><b><sup>&#174;</sup></b></font> and began marketing Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> in the second quarter of 2009. &nbsp;We currently anticipate that the near term growth of Strativa will be based largely on focusing on the sales and marketing efforts behind our current brand products. &nbsp;In the longer term, we will continue to consider strategic product or business acquisitions or licensing arrangements to expand Strativa&#146;s brand product line in supportive care and adjacent commercial areas. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:24px">&nbsp;</p><a name=OLE_LINK3> <p style="FONT-SIZE:10.5pt; MARGIN:0px"><b>ITEM 1A. &nbsp;<u>Risk Factors </u></b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The pharmaceutical industry is a fast-paced, highly competitive environment with many factors that influence the ability of a company to successfully commercialize a product. &nbsp;Many of these factors are beyond our control and are, therefore, difficult to predict. &nbsp;The following section sets forth the principal risks to our business activities and condition (financial or otherwise) and prospects. &nbsp;These risks, along with others, have the potential to materially and adversely affect our business, financial position, results of operations and prospects. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="FONT-SIZE:10.5pt; &nbsp;Any future acquisitions may involve numerous risks, including but not limited to the types of risks set forth above with respect to the Anchen and Edict acquisitions. &nbsp;</p> <p requisite regulatory approvals for such products in a timely manner;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN:0px"><br><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>15</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <hr size=1 noshade style="MARGIN-BOTTOM:9px; PADDING-TOP:9px"> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FONT-SIZE:4pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-4pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always" /> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; style="PADDING-LEFT:60px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">delays or unanticipated costs, including delays associated with the FDA listing and/or approval process; and</p> <p style="CLEAR:left;
