MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On February 2, 2011, Somaxon Pharmaceuticals filed a lawsuit against us in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. &nbsp;The complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent No. 6,211,229 because we submitted an ANDA with a Paragraph IV certification to the FDA for approval of oral tablets of 3 mg equivalent and 6 mg equivalent doxepin hydrochloride. &nbsp;We filed our answer on February&nbsp;23, 2011. &nbsp;Our case has been consolidated in the same Court with those of the other defendants who filed ANDAs on this product. &nbsp;The Court has scheduled fact discovery to end on April 6, 2012; expert discovery to end on August 17, 2012; the end of <i>Markman</i> briefing for October 12, 2012; and a trial date of December 10, 2012. &nbsp;We intend to defend this action vigorously. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On March 23, 2011, we filed a declaratory judgment action against UCB, Inc. and UCB Pharma SA (collectively &#147;UCB&#148;) in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania requesting that the Court render a judgment of invalidity and/or non-infringement of U.S. Patent Nos. 7,858,122 and 7,863,316 in view of our intent to market levetiracetam extended release oral tablets, 500 mg and 750 mg pursuant to our filed ANDA that was accompanied by a Paragraph IV certification. On August 22, 2011, the parties entered into a stipulated dismissal of the case pursuant to a settlement agreement that allowed Par to launch its generic levetiracetam extended release product on September 13, 2011 subject to certain confidential conditions.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On September 1, 2011, we, along with EDT Pharma Holdings Ltd. (now known as Alkermes Pharma Ireland Limited) (Elan), filed a complaint against TWi Pharmaceuticals, Inc. of Taiwan in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland and another complaint against TWi on September 2, 2011, in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois. &nbsp;In both complaints, Elan and we allege infringement of U.S. Patent No. 7,101,576 (expiration April 22, 2024) in view of the notice letter we received from TWi stating that TWi had filed an ANDA, accompanied by a Paragraph IV certification, seeking approval for a generic version of Megace&#174; ES. &nbsp;We are at present aware of no other generic filers. &nbsp;On November 15, 2011, the Court scheduled the end of fact discovery for September 1, 2012; the end of expert discovery for December 15, 2012; and a 5-7 day bench trial for October 7, 2013. &nbsp;We intend to prosecute this infringement case vigorously.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On April 8, 2010, AstraZeneca filed a lawsuit against Anchen Incorporated (now a subsidiary of Par Pharmaceutical, Inc.) in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey. &nbsp;The complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent No. 5,948,437 for submitting an ANDA with a Paragraph IV certification to the FDA for approval of extended-release oral tablets of 150, 200, 300, and 400 mg quetiapine. &nbsp;A <i>Markman </i>hearing was conducted on November 30, 2010 and a bench trial was held from October 3-19, 2011. &nbsp;We are awaiting a decision and will continue to defend this action vigorously.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On June 10, 2010, Genzyme Corporation filed a lawsuit against Anchen in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. &nbsp;The complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent Nos. 5,602,116, and 6,903,083 for submitting an ANDA with a Paragraph IV certification to the FDA for approval of oral capsules of 0.5, 1, and 2.5 mcg doxercalciferol. &nbsp;A bench trial was conducted from November&nbsp;14-18, 2011. &nbsp;We are awaiting a decision and will continue to defend this action vigorously.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On June 14, 2010, Abbott Laboratories and Fournier Laboratories Ireland Ltd. filed a lawsuit against Anchen in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey. &nbsp;The complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent No. 7,259,186 for submitting an ANDA with a Paragraph IV certification to the FDA for approval of delayed-release oral capsules of EQ 45 and EQ 135 mg choline fenofibrate. &nbsp;A <i>Markman</i> hearing was held May 24, 2011, and a final pre-trial conference was held November 16, 2011. &nbsp;On October 24, 2011, we filed a motion for summary judgment of invalidity, which is currently pending before the Court. &nbsp;We will continue to defend this action vigorously. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On January 12, 2011, GlaxoSmithKline, LLC filed a lawsuit against Anchen in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. &nbsp;The complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent No. 5,565,467 for submitting an ANDA with a Paragraph IV certification to the FDA for approval of an oral capsule of 0.5 mg dutasteride and an oral capsule of 0.5/0.4 mg dutasteride/tamsulosin. &nbsp;On November 30, 2011, the court confirmed that the bench trial for this case is set for October 22, 2012. &nbsp;We will continue to defend this action vigorously.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On September 9, 2011, Flamel Technologies, S.A. filed a lawsuit against Anchen in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland. &nbsp;The complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent No. 6,022,562 for submitting an ANDA with a Paragraph IV certification to the FDA for approval of extended-release oral capsules of 10, 20, 40, and 80 mg carvedilol. &nbsp;The complaint was served on us on January 12, 2012, and we filed our answer on January 30, 2012. &nbsp;We will defend this action vigorously.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt" align=center>30</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt"> <hr> <p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; LINE-HEIGHT:10.8pt">On October 28, 2011, Astra Zeneca, Pozen, Inc., and KBI-E Inc., filed a lawsuit against Anchen in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey. &nbsp;The complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent Nos. 6,926,907; 6,369,085; 7,411,070; and 7,745,466 for submitting an ANDA with a Paragraph IV certification to the FDA for approval of delayed-release oral tablets of 375/20 and 500/20 mg naproxen/esomeprazole magnesium. &nbsp;We filed our answer on December 12, 2011. &nbsp;We will continue to defend this action vigorously. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px"><b>Industry Related Matters &nbsp;</b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Beginning in September 2003, we, along with numerous other pharmaceutical companies, have been named as a defendant in actions brought by a number of state Attorneys General and municipal bodies within the state of New York, as well as a federal <i>qui tam </i>action brought on behalf of the United States by the pharmacy Ven-A-Care of the Florida Keys, Inc. ("Ven-A-Care") alleging generally that the defendants defrauded the state Medicaid systems by purportedly reporting &#147;Average Wholesale Prices&#148; (&#147;AWP&#148;) and/or &#147;Wholesale Acquisition Costs&#148; that exceeded the actual selling price of the defendants&#146; prescription drugs.&nbsp; To date, we have been named as a defendant in substantially similar civil law suits filed by the Attorneys General of Alabama, Alaska, Florida, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas, Utah and Wisconsin, and also by the city of New York, 46 counties across New York State and Ven-A-Care.&nbsp; These cases generally seek some combination of actual damages, and/or double damages, treble damages, compensatory damages, statutory damages, civil penalties, disgorgement of excessive profits, restitution, disbursements, counsel fees and costs, litigation expenses, investigative costs, injunctive relief, punitive damages, imposition of a constructive trust, accounting of profits or gains derived through the alleged conduct, expert fees, interest and other relief that the court deems proper.&nbsp; In the Utah suit, the time for responding to the complaint has not yet elapsed. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Hawaii suit was settled on August 25, 2010 for $2,250 thousand. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Massachusetts suit was settled on December 17, 2010 for $500 thousand. &nbsp;The Alabama suit was settled on January 5, 2011 for $2,500 thousand. &nbsp;The Idaho suit was settled on March 25, 2011 for $1,700 thousand. &nbsp;On August 24, 2011, we settled claims brought by Ven-A-Care, Texas, and Florida, under federal and state law, as well as Alaska, South Carolina, and Kentucky under state law, for $154,000 thousand. &nbsp;The settlement resolved the lawsuit relating to federal contributions to state Medicaid programs in 49 states (excluding Illinois), and claims of Texas, Florida, Alaska, South Carolina and Kentucky relating to their Medicaid programs. The settlement eliminated the majority of the alleged damages asserted against us in the various drug pricing litigations and removed all trials that had been scheduled. &nbsp;We paid the $154,000 thousand settlement amount during the third quarter of 2011. &nbsp;On June 2, 2011, we reached a settlement in principle to resolve claims brought by the city of New York, New York Counties and the state of Iowa under respective state law for $23,000 thousand. &nbsp;The Mississippi suit was settled on September 1, 2011 for $3,600 thousand. &nbsp;On October 18, 2011, we reached an agreement in principle to settle the Oklahoma suit for $884 thousand. &nbsp;The remaining matters have yet to be scheduled for trial. &nbsp;We have accrued a $37,800 thousand reserve under the caption &#147;Accrued legal settlements&#148; on our consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2011, in connection with the June 2, 2011 settlement in principle and the remaining AWP actions. &nbsp;In each of the remaining matters, we have either moved to dismiss the complaints or answered the complaints denying liability.&nbsp; We will continue to defend or explore settlement opportunities in other jurisdictions as we feel are in our best interest under the circumstances presented in those jurisdictions. &nbsp;However, we can give no assurance that we will be able to settle the remaining actions on terms that we deem reasonable, or that such settlements or adverse judgments, if entered, will not exceed the amount of the reserve.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The Attorneys General of Florida, Indiana and Virginia and the United States Office of Personnel Management (the &#147;USOPM&#148;) have issued subpoenas, and the Attorneys General of Michigan, Tennessee, Texas, and Utah have issued civil investigative demands, to us.&nbsp; The demands generally request documents and information pertaining to allegations that certain of our sales and marketing practices caused pharmacies to substitute ranitidine capsules for ranitidine tablets, fluoxetine tablets for fluoxetine capsules, and two 7.5 mg buspirone tablets for one 15 mg buspirone tablet, under circumstances in which some state Medicaid programs at various times reimbursed the new dosage form at a higher rate than the dosage form being substituted.&nbsp; We have provided documents in response to these subpoenas to the respective Attorneys General and the USOPM. &nbsp;The aforementioned subpoenas and civil investigative demands culminated in the federal and state law <i>qui tam</i> action brought on behalf of the United States and several states by Bernard Lisitza. &nbsp;The complaint was unsealed on August 30, 2011. &nbsp;The United States intervened in this action on July 8, 2011 and filed a separate complaint on September 9, 2011, alleging claims for violations of the Federal False Claims Act and common law fraud. &nbsp;We intend to vigorously defend this lawsuit. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">We have also been named a defendant in a putative federal class action brought by the United Food and Commercial Workers Unions and Employers Midwest Health Benefits Fund (&#147;UFCW&#148;) under the Federal Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act alleging the same general conduct as set forth in the preceding paragraph. &nbsp;The time for responding to the complaint filed by UFCW has not yet elapsed. &nbsp;We intend to vigorously defend this lawsuit.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px"><b>Department of Justice Matter</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">On March 19, 2009, we were served with a subpoena by the Department of Justice requesting documents related to Strativa&#146;s marketing of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES.&nbsp; The subpoena indicated that the Department of Justice is currently investigating promotional practices in the sales and marketing of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES.&nbsp; We believe that our marketing of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES has complied with all applicable laws and we have provided, or are in the process of providing, documents in response to this subpoena to the Department of Justice and will continue to cooperate with the Department of Justice in this inquiry if called upon to do so. &nbsp;Investigations of this type often result in settlements, including&nbsp;monetary amounts based on an agreed upon percentage of sales of the product at issue in the investigation. </p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px" align=center>31</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px"> <hr> <p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:13px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px"><b>Declaratory Judgment</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">On October 14, 2011, we filed a declaratory complaint and a motion for preliminary injunction in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking to preserve our First Amendment right to provide truthful information to physicians and other healthcare providers about the FDA-approved, on-label use of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES. </p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; We intend to defend or, in cases where we are the plaintiff, to prosecute these litigations vigorously.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p><a name=OLE_LINK7> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center><font style=BACKGROUND-COLOR:#ffffff><b>PART II</b></font></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p><a name=OLE_LINK8> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>ITEM 5. &nbsp;<u>Market for Registrant&#146;s Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities</u></b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:82px; TEXT-INDENT:32px"><font style=BACKGROUND-COLOR:#ffffff><i>(a)</i></font></p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:82px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px"><font style=BACKGROUND-COLOR:#ffffff><i>Market information.</i></font><font style=BACKGROUND-COLOR:#ffffff>&nbsp;&nbsp;Our Common Stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange (the &#147;NYSE&#148;) (ticker symbol: PRX). TEXT-INDENT:48px">Refer to Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Note 2 &#150; &#147;Anchen Acquisition&#148; contained elsewhere in this Form 10-K for details of our 2011 acquisition that was the primary reason for the increase in Total assets and Long-term debt, less current portion above. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p><a name=OLE_LINK10> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:60px"><b>ITEM 7.</b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px" align=justify><b><u>Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</u></b></p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN:0px"><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The following discussion should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements contained elsewhere in this Form 10-K. &nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>OVERVIEW </b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Par Pharmaceutical Companies, Inc. operates primarily in the United States as two business segments, our generic products division (&#147;Par Pharmaceutical&#148; or &#147;Par&#148;) for the development, manufacture and distribution of generic pharmaceuticals, and Strativa Pharmaceuticals (&#147;Strativa&#148;), our branded products division. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The introduction of new products at prices that generate adequate gross margins is critical to our ability to generate economic value and ultimately the creation of adequate returns for our stockholders. &nbsp;Par Pharmaceutical, our generic products division, creates economic value by optimizing our current generic product portfolio and our pipeline of potential high-value first-to-file and first-to-market generic products. &nbsp;Par Pharmaceutical is an attractive business partner because of its strong commercialization track record and presence in the generic trade. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">On November 17, 2011, we completed our acquisition of Anchen Incorporated and its subsidiary Anchen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (collectively referred to as &#147;Anchen&#148;), a privately held generic pharmaceutical company. &nbsp;The Anchen assets we acquired include five currently marketed generic products, numerous in-process research and development products, which include a pipeline of 29 filed ANDAs, a workforce of approximately 200 employees and leased facilities with manufacturing capabilities and research and development capabilities. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, we also had a then-pending acquisition of Edict Pharmaceuticals Private Limited (&#147;Edict&#148;), a Chennai, India-based developer and manufacturer of generic pharmaceuticals. &nbsp;The Edict assets include numerous in-process research and development products, which includes a pipeline of 11 filed ANDAs, a workforce of approximately 100 employees and a facility with manufacturing capabilities and research and development capabilities. &nbsp;We closed our acquisition of Edict on February 17, 2012. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In addition to our acquisitions, Par&#146;s 2011 achievements included eight launches (including generic versions of Entocort<sup>&#174;</sup> EC, Rythmol SR<sup>&#174;</sup>, and Lotrel<sup>&#174;</sup>), execution of several business development agreements, passing all FDA inspections, and settling three Paragraph IV litigations. &nbsp;As a result, we believe we are well positioned to compete in the generic marketplace over the long term. &nbsp;We target high-value, first-to-file Paragraph IVs or first&#150;to-market product opportunities. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, we had 72 total filed ANDAs that represented over $20 billion of combined branded product sales. &nbsp;These ANDA filings included 19 confirmed first-to-files and four potential first-to-market product opportunities. &nbsp;Generally, products that we have developed internally contribute higher gross margin percentages than products that we sell under supply and distribution agreements, because under such agreements, we typically pay a percentage of the gross or net profits (or a percentage of sales) to our strategic partners. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Strativa acquired the worldwide rights to Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> Nasal Spray in 2009. &nbsp;Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> Nasal Spray is an FDA-approved prescription vitamin B12 treatment indicated for maintenance of remission in certain pernicious anemia patients, as well as a supplement for a variety of B12 deficiencies. &nbsp;It is the first and currently only once-weekly, self-administered alternative to B12 injections. &nbsp;We project Nascobal<sup>&#174; </sup>Nasal Spray to reach peak annual sales in a range from $40 million to $50 million. &nbsp;In June 2011, we announced our plans to resize Strativa as part of a strategic assessment. &nbsp;We reduced our Strativa workforce by approximately 90 people. &nbsp;The remaining Strativa sales force focus their marketing efforts on Megace<sup>&#174; </sup>ES and Nascobal<sup>&#174; </sup>Nasal Spray. &nbsp;In July 2011, we received a notice letter from a generic pharmaceutical manufacturer advising that&nbsp;it has filed&nbsp;an Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) with the U.S. FDA containing a Paragraph IV certification referencing Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES. &nbsp;Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES is protected by Alkermes Pharma Ireland Limited (Elan)&#146;s U.S. Patents 6,592,903 and 7,101,576.&nbsp; We intend, with Elan, to&nbsp;investigate the Paragraph IV certification and ANDA, and to enforce&nbsp;Elan&#146;s patents, which expire in 2020 and 2024, respectively, as appropriate. &nbsp;Together with Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES and the current level of personnel deployed in the field, we believe Strativa will generate cash inflows in excess of cash outflows into the foreseeable future. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Sales and gross margins of our products depend principally on (i)&nbsp;our ability to introduce new generic and brand products and the introduction of other generic and brand products in direct competition with our products; (ii)&nbsp;the ability of generic competitors to quickly enter the market after our relevant patent or exclusivity periods expire, or during our exclusivity periods with authorized generic products, diminishing the amount and duration of significant profits we generate from any one product; (iii)&nbsp;the pricing practices of competitors and the removal of competing products from the market; (iv)&nbsp;the continuation of our existing license, supply and distribution agreements and our ability to enter into new agreements; (v)&nbsp;the consolidation among distribution outlets through mergers, acquisitions and the formation of buying groups; (vi)&nbsp;the willingness of generic drug customers, including wholesale and retail customers, to switch among drugs of different generic pharmaceutical manufacturers; (vii)&nbsp;our ability to procure approval of ANDAs and NDAs and the timing and success of our future new product launches; (viii)&nbsp;our ability to obtain marketing exclusivity periods for our generic products; (ix)&nbsp;our ability to maintain patent protection of our brand products; (x)&nbsp;the extent of market penetration for our existing product line; (xi)&nbsp;customer satisfaction with the level, quality and amount of our customer service; and (xii)&nbsp;the market acceptance of our recently introduced branded product (Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> Nasal Spray) and the successful development and commercialization of any future in-licensed branded product pipeline. </p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Net sales and gross margins derived from generic pharmaceutical products often follow a pattern based on regulatory and competitive factors that we believe to be unique to the generic pharmaceutical industry. &nbsp;As the patent(s) for a brand name product and the related exclusivity period(s) expire, the first generic manufacturer to receive regulatory approval from the FDA for a generic equivalent of the product is often able to capture a substantial share of the market. &nbsp;At that time, however, the brand company may license the right to distribute an &#147;authorized generic&#148; product to a competing generic company. &nbsp;As additional generic manufacturers receive regulatory approvals for competing products, the market share and the price of those products have typically declined - often significantly - depending on several factors, including the number of competitors, the price of the brand product and the pricing strategy of the new competitors. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Net sales and gross margins derived from brand pharmaceutical products typically follow a different pattern. &nbsp;Sellers of brand pharmaceutical products benefit from years of being the exclusive supplier to the market due to patent protections for the brand products. &nbsp;The benefits include significantly higher gross margins relative to sellers of generic pharmaceutical products. &nbsp;However, commercializing brand pharmaceutical products is more costly than generic pharmaceutical products. &nbsp;Sellers of brand pharmaceutical products often have increased infrastructure costs relative to sellers of generic pharmaceutical products and make significant investments in the development and/or licensing of these products without a guarantee that these expenditures will result in the successful development or launch of brand products that will prove to be commercially successful. &nbsp;Selling brand products also tends to require greater sales and marketing expenses to create a market for the products than is necessary with respect to the sale of generic products. &nbsp;Just as our generic products take market share away from the corresponding branded products, we confront the same competitive pressures from other generic pharmaceutical companies when we sell our branded products. &nbsp;Specifically, after patent protections expire, or after a successful challenge to the patents protecting one of our brand products, generic products can be sold in the market at a significantly lower price than the branded version, and, where available, may be required or encouraged in preference to the branded version under third party reimbursement programs, or substituted by pharmacies for branded versions by law. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px" align=center>36</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:36px"> <hr> <p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:24px"><i>Healthcare Reform Impacts</i></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">On March 23, 2010, President Obama signed into law the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) and on March 30, 2010, President Obama signed into law the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act, which includes a number of changes to the PPACA. &nbsp;These laws are hereafter referred to as &#147;healthcare reform&#148; or the &#147;Acts.&#148; &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">A number of provisions of healthcare reform have had and will continue to have a negative impact on the price of our products sold to U.S. government entities. &nbsp;The significant provisions that impacted net revenues, gross margin and net income for the years ended December 31, 2011 and 2010 include, but are not limited to, the following (all items were effective January 1, 2010 unless otherwise noted): &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:52px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:52px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Increase in the Medicaid rebate rate. &nbsp;The base rebate rate on sales of brand drugs (Strativa) and authorized generics (Par) into the Medicaid channel was increased from 15.1% of AMP (average manufacturer price) to 23.1% of AMP. &nbsp;The base rebate on sales of multisource generic products (Par) into the Medicaid channel was increased from 11% of AMP to 13% of AMP. &nbsp;The base rebate is one component of the calculation for branded drugs and authorized generics, and may or may not result in an increase in rebates for a particular product. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:52px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:52px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Effective March 23, 2010, there was an extension of Medicaid rebates to drugs consumed by patients enrolled in Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MMCOs). &nbsp;Prior to healthcare reform, MMCOs were not entitled to Medicaid rebates, as the drug benefit was independently managed by the commercial managed care entity. &nbsp;Given our current product portfolio, which is weighted more toward generic products, our exposure to commercial rebates for patients enrolled in MMCOs was low prior to March 23, 2010. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:52px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:52px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Increased Medicaid rebates for products defined as a line extension through application of an inflation penalty back to the original formulation price.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:52px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:52px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Expansion of the number of entities qualifying for Public Health System (PHS) status and therefore eligible to receive PHS pricing, which is typically equal to the net Medicaid price after rebates. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:52px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:52px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Revisions to the AMP calculation, effective October 1, 2010. &nbsp;This provision had a negligible impact on net revenues and gross margins for the year ended December 31, 2011. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:52px; TEXT-INDENT:28px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:52px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Change in the Federal Upper Limit as it relates to the pharmacy reimbursement of multisource drugs. This provision is expected to reduce the Medicaid funding from the federal government. &nbsp;While it is impractical to quantify the impact of the provision, it is expected to result in increased pressure at the state level to drive Medicaid utilization to low cost alternatives such as generic products.</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN:0px"><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2011, the following provisions went into effect:</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:54px; TEXT-INDENT:36px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:60px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">An annual, non tax deductible, pharmaceutical fee assessed by the Secretary of the Treasury on any manufacturer or importer with gross receipts from the sale of branded prescription and authorized generic drugs to the following government programs and entities: Medicare Part D, Medicare Part B, Medicaid, Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Defense, and Tricare. &nbsp;The total pharmaceutical fee, which was set at $2.5 billion for 2011, was allocated across the pharmaceutical industry based upon relative market share into these programs. &nbsp;The total fee increases each year thereafter, reaching $4.1 billion in 2018.</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:60px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:60px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px" align=center>37</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:60px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px"> <hr> <p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:60px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px"><br><br>The market share calculation utilized to allocate the fee is calculated utilizing prior year&#146;s sales statistics. &nbsp;The impact of the pharmaceutical fee on our 2011 net income was approximately $2.1 million. &nbsp;In addition, the year to year impact of this provision of healthcare reform will be highly variable depending on:</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:96px; TEXT-INDENT:72px; FONT-FAMILY:Courier New">o</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:96px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">the volume of Par&#146;s sales of authorized generics, which can vary dramatically based upon our ability to continue to secure authorized generic business development opportunities, </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:96px; TEXT-INDENT:72px; FONT-FAMILY:Courier New">o</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:96px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">the volume of Strativa&#146;s sales of brand products, and &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:96px; TEXT-INDENT:72px; FONT-FAMILY:Courier New">o</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:96px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">our ability to share portions of this fee with partners under pre-existing and future distribution agreements. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">A 50% discount on cost for certain Medicare Part D beneficiaries for certain drugs, including branded and authorized generic pharmaceuticals, purchased during the Part D Medicare coverage gap (commonly referred to as the &#147;donut hole&#148;). &nbsp;&nbsp;The 2011 gross margin impact of this provision for Par was $1.8 million and Strativa was $0.8 million. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Additionally, the publication of monthly weighted average AMP by therapeutic class and retail price surveys began in September 2011. &nbsp;&nbsp;It is not practical to isolate the impact of this provision on 2011 net revenues or gross margin. &nbsp;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">For the year ended December 31, 2011, the impact of healthcare reform resulted in decreases of approximately $16.8 million to our net revenue, approximately $7.3 million to our gross margin, and approximately $9.5 million to our net income. &nbsp;The gross margin impact of these provisions is highly dependent upon product sales mix between products that are partnered with third parties and non-partnered products. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Any potential impact of healthcare reform on the future demand for our products is not determinable at this time. &nbsp;Any potential future impact on demand could differ between our Par and Strativa divisions, as well as between individual products within each division. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:13px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:12px; FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman" align=justify><b>Par Pharmaceutical -</b><font style="FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman"><b> Generic Products Division</b></font></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Our strategy for our generic products division is to continue to differentiate ourselves by carefully choosing opportunities with minimal competition (<i>e.g</i>., first-to-file and first-to-market products).&nbsp; By leveraging our expertise in research and development, manufacturing and distribution, and business development, we are able to effectively and efficiently pursue these opportunities and support our partners.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">During the year ended December 31, 2011, our generic business net revenues and gross margin were concentrated in a few products. &nbsp;The top nine generic products (metoprolol succinate ER (metoprolol), budesonide, propafenone, sumatriptan, chlorpheniramine/hydrocodone, amlodipine and benazepril HCl dronabinol, tramadol ER, and meclizine) accounted for approximately 65% of total consolidated revenues and approximately 50% of total consolidated gross margins in the year ended December 31, 2011. </p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We began selling metoprolol in the fourth quarter of 2006 as the authorized generic distributor pursuant to a supply and distribution agreement with AstraZeneca.&nbsp; From the fourth quarter of 2008 throughout the first two quarters of 2009, we were the sole distributor of generic metoprolol, which resulted in increased volume of units sold coupled with a price increase commensurate with being the sole generic distributor.&nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning in August 2009, competitors have entered the market at various times on various of the four SKUs (packaging sizes) of the product, and we are no longer the sole distributor of any SKU of the product. &nbsp;Our sales volume and unit price for metoprolol were adversely impacted subsequent to each entry of a competitor&#146;s SKU into the market. &nbsp;On December&nbsp;16, 2011, a third competitor received FDA approval for all four strengths of metoprolol and our sales volume and unit price were adversely impacted. &nbsp;Additional competitors on any or all of the four SKUs will result in additional declines in sales volume and unit price, which would negatively impact our revenues and gross margins. &nbsp;As the authorized generic distributor for metoprolol, we do not control the manufacturing of the product, and any disruption in supply due to manufacturing or transportation issues could also have a negative effect on our revenues and gross margins. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In 2008, we launched generic versions of Imitrex<sup>&#174;</sup> (sumatriptan) injection 4mg and 6mg starter kits and 4mg and 6mg prefilled syringe cartridges pursuant to a supply and distribution agreement with GlaxoSmithKline plc (&#147;GSK&#148;).&nbsp; On August 1, 2011, an additional competitor launched a single strength of sumatriptan. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, we believe we were the sole generic distributor of two SKUs with two competitors on the 6mg strength. &nbsp;We believe our future sales volume and unit price for sumatriptan may be adversely impacted by any additional competition. &nbsp;Our supply agreement with GSK ended in November 2011. &nbsp;Under the terms of that agreement we can continue to distribute our existing inventory until depleted. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">In August 2009, we launched clonidine TDS, the generic version of Boehringer Ingelheim&#146;s Catapres TTS<sup>&#174;</sup>. &nbsp;The product was manufactured by Aveva Drug Delivery Systems, Inc., our third party development partner, with whom we have a profit sharing arrangement. &nbsp;In April 2011, Aveva discontinued manufacturing clonidine due to a May 2010 Warning Letter received from the FDA citing potential violations of Good Manufacturing Practices at Aveva&#146;s manufacturing facility, and the product was voluntarily withdrawn from the distribution channel. &nbsp;Because we have no supply, we have discontinued selling the product.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px" align=center>38</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px"> <hr> <p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We reintroduced meclizine HCl tablets in 12.5mg and 25mg strengths in 2008. &nbsp;From the beginning of 2009 to May 2010, we were the exclusive supplier of this generic product. &nbsp;In June 2010, a competitor entered this market, and in July 2011, a second competitor entered this market. &nbsp;This new competition negatively impacted our sales and gross margins for meclizine. &nbsp;Any additional competition could result in significant additional declines in sales volume and unit price, which may negatively impact our revenues and gross margins. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In 2008, we launched dronabinol in 2.5mg, 5mg and 10mg strengths in soft gel capsules. &nbsp;We believe we are one of two generic distributors of dronabinol. &nbsp;We share net product margin, as contractually defined, with SVC Pharma LP, an affiliate of Rhodes Technologies. &nbsp;We do not control the manufacturing of the product, and any disruption in supply due to manufacturing or transportation issues, or additional competition on the product, could have a negative effect on our revenues and gross margins. &nbsp;The remaining net book value of the associated intangible asset was $0.7 million at December 31, 2011, and will be amortized over approximately two years. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">In November 2009, we launched tramadol ER, the generic version of Ultram<sup>&#174;</sup> ER, after a favorable court ruling in the related patent matter. &nbsp;We believe we are one of two competitors in this market, with the other competitor being the authorized generic. &nbsp;Additional competitors will result in declines in sales volume and unit price, which would negatively impact our revenues and gross margins. &nbsp;We manufacture and distribute this product. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In July 2010, we launched two strengths of omeprazole/sodium bicarbonate capsules, the generic version of Zegerid<sup>&#174;</sup>. &nbsp;We were awarded 180 days of marketing exclusivity for being the first to file an ANDA containing a paragraph IV certification for these two strengths of the product. &nbsp;We are now one of two competitors in this market, with the other competitor being the authorized generic. &nbsp;Omeprazole/sodium bicarbonate capsules had been the subject of litigation in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, but in April 2010, the Court ruled in our favor, finding that the related patents were invalid as being obvious and without adequate written description.&nbsp; The case is currently on appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. &nbsp;We will continue to vigorously defend the appeal. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">On October 5, 2010, our licensing partner, Tris Pharma, Inc., received final FDA approval for its ANDA for hydrocodone polistirex and chlorpheniramine polistirex (CIII) extended-release (ER) oral suspension (equivalent to 10 mg of hydrocodone bitartrate and 8 mg of chlorpheniramine maleate per 5 mL), a generic version of UCB Manufacturing, Inc.&#146;s Tussionex<sup>&#174;</sup>.&nbsp; We participate in a profit sharing arrangement with Tris based on our commercial sale of generic Tussionex<sup>&#174;</sup>.&nbsp; We commenced a limited launch of <a name=OLE_LINK33><a name=OLE_LINK31>generic Tussionex<sup>&#174;</sup> on October 5, 2010.&nbsp; Our market share will continue to be limited for the foreseeable future by Drug Enforcement Administration regulations concerning allowable commercial quantities of controlled substances like hydrocodone, which is contained in generic Tussionex<sup>&#174;</sup>.&nbsp; We do not control the manufacturing of the product, and any disruption in supply due to manufacturing or transportation issues could also have a negative effect on our revenues and gross margins. &nbsp;In October 2010, UCB filed a complaint naming us, our development partner Tris Pharma, and Tris Pharma&#146;s head of research and development as defendants.&nbsp; The complaint alleged that Tris and its head of research and development misappropriated UCB&#146;s trade secrets and, by their actions, breached contracts and agreements to which they were bound.&nbsp; The complaint further alleges unfair competition against the defendants relating to the parties&#146; manufacture and marketing of generic Tussionex<sup>&#174;</sup>.&nbsp; On October 6, 2010, the Court denied UCB&#146;s petition for a temporary restraining order and set a schedule for discovery during which UCB must substantiate its claims. &nbsp;On December 23, 2010, the Court denied UCB&#146;s motion for a preliminary injunction, ruling that UCB&#146;s alleged trade secrets were known to the public and not misappropriated.&nbsp; On June 2, 2011, the Court granted Tris&#146;s motion for summary judgment dismissing UCB&#146;s claims, and UCB appealed the Court&#146;s order on June 22, 2011. &nbsp;We intend to vigorously defend the appeal by UCB. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We began selling propafenone, the generic version of Rythmol<sup>&#174; </sup>SR, in January 2011. &nbsp;We were awarded 180 days of marketing exclusivity for being the first to file an ANDA containing a paragraph IV certification for this product. &nbsp;We manufacture and distribute this product. &nbsp;We believe we remained the single source generic supplier for this product as of December 31, 2011. &nbsp;The market entry of any competition on this product will result in declines in sales volume and unit price, which would negatively impact our revenues and gross margins. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We began selling amlodipine and benazepril, the generic version of Lotrel<sup>&#174;</sup>, in January 2011. &nbsp;We were awarded 180 days of marketing exclusivity for being the first to file an ANDA containing a paragraph IV certification for this product. &nbsp;Multiple competitors entered the market for this product in July 2011, and our sales volume and unit price were adversely affected. &nbsp;We manufacture and distribute this product and share net product margin, as contractually defined, with a partner. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We began selling budesonide, the generic version of Entocort<sup> &#174; </sup>EC, in June 2011 as the authorized generic distributor pursuant to a supply and distribution agreement with AstraZeneca. &nbsp;&nbsp;We are one of two competitors in this market. &nbsp;As the authorized generic distributor for budesonide, we do not control the manufacturing of the product, and any disruption in supply due to manufacturing or transportation issues, as well as additional competition, could have a negative effect on our revenues and gross margins. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In addition, our investments in generic product development, including projects with development partners, are expected to yield approximately 13 to 17 new ANDA filings during each of 2012, 2013 and 2014. &nbsp;These ANDA filings are expected to lead to product launches based on one or more of the following: expiry of the relevant 30-month stay period; patent expiry date; and expiry of regulatory exclusivity. &nbsp;However, such potential product launches may be delayed or may not occur due to various circumstances, including extended litigation, outstanding citizens petitions, other regulatory requirements set forth by the FDA, and stays of litigation. &nbsp;These ANDA filings would be significant mileposts for us, as we expect many of these potential products to be first-to-file/first-to-market opportunities with gross margins in excess of the average of our current portfolio. &nbsp;We or our strategic partners had approximately 72 ANDAs pending with the FDA, which include 19 first-to-file and four first-to-market opportunities as of December&nbsp;31, 2011. &nbsp;No assurances can be given that we or any of our strategic partners will successfully complete the development of any of these potential products either under development or proposed for development, that regulatory approvals will be granted for any such product, that any approved product will be produced in commercial quantities or sold profitably. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px" align=center>39</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px"> <hr> <p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:12px" align=justify><b>Strativa Pharmaceuticals - Branded Products Division </b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">For Strativa, in the near term we will continue to invest in the marketing and sales of our existing products (Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES and Nascobal<sup>&#174; </sup>Nasal Spray). &nbsp;In addition, in the longer term, we will continue to consider new strategic licenses and acquisitions to expand Strativa&#146;s presence in supportive care and adjacent commercial areas. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In July 2005, we received FDA approval for our first NDA, and immediately began marketing Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES (megestrol acetate) oral suspension. &nbsp;Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES is indicated for the treatment of anorexia, cachexia or any unexplained significant weight loss in patients with a diagnosis of AIDS and utilizes the Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> brand name that we have licensed from Bristol-Myers Squibb Company. &nbsp;The remaining net book value of the trademark was $0.9 million at December 31, 2011, and will be amortized over approximately one year. &nbsp;We promoted Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES as our primary brand product from 2005 through March 2009. &nbsp;With the acquisition of Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> in March 2009, Strativa increased its sales force and turned its focus on marketing both products. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In July 2011, we received a notice letter from a generic pharmaceutical manufacturer, advising that&nbsp;it has filed&nbsp;an Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) with the U.S. FDA containing a Paragraph IV certification referencing Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES. &nbsp;&nbsp;Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES is protected by Alkermes Pharma Ireland Limited (Elan)&#146;s U.S. Patents 6,592,903 and 7,101,576.&nbsp; We intend, with Elan, to&nbsp;investigate the Paragraph IV certification and ANDA, and to enforce&nbsp;Elan&#146;s patents, which expire in 2020 and 2024, respectively, as appropriate. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">On March 31, 2009, we acquired the worldwide rights to Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> (cyanocobalamin, USP) Nasal Spray from QOL Medical, LLC. &nbsp;Under the terms of the all cash transaction, we paid QOL Medical $54.5 million for the worldwide rights to Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup>.&nbsp; We manufacture Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup> with assets acquired on March 31, 2009 from MDRNA, Inc. &nbsp;The remaining net book value of the related intangible asset was $42.2 million at December 31, 2011, and will be amortized over approximately 9 years. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In January 2011, we completed a modest reorganization of the Strativa management team (eliminating approximately ten positions) and refined our sales and marketing plan for each of Strativa&#146;s then-marketed products as part of our on-going efforts to maximize the value and potential of our existing product portfolio. &nbsp;We announced that the President of Strativa Pharmaceuticals resigned and that effective January 31, 2011, Patrick G. LePore, the Chairman and CEO, assumed day-to-day oversight of Strativa on an interim basis. &nbsp;In November 2011, Paul V. Campanelli, Chief Operating Officer and President, Par Pharmaceutical, assumed responsibility for Strativa. &nbsp;We have taken steps to further align the Strativa home office sales and marketing team with the objectives of our sales force and to leverage the relevant expertise and experience within our Par Pharmaceutical generics division. &nbsp;In conjunction with these events, we recalibrated our target sales for our currently marketed products. &nbsp;Further information regarding such forecasts can be found in our Form 8-K filed January 6, 2012. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px; LINE-HEIGHT:12pt">In June 2011, we announced our plans to resize Strativa as part of a strategic assessment. &nbsp;We reduced our Strativa workforce by approximately 90 people. &nbsp;The remaining Strativa sales force focus their marketing efforts on Megace<sup>&#174; </sup>ES and Nascobal<sup>&#174; </sup>Nasal Spray. &nbsp;The intangible assets related to products no longer a priority for our remaining Strativa sales force were fully impaired by these actions. &nbsp;In July 2011, Strativa returned the U.S. commercialization rights for Zuplenz<sup>&#174; </sup>to MonoSol, as part of the resizing of Strativa. &nbsp;In September 2011, Strativa executed a termination agreement with BioAlliance returning all Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> rights and obligations to BioAlliance. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px"><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:12px"><b><i>OTHER CONSIDERATIONS</i></b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">In addition to the substantial costs of product development, we may incur significant legal costs in bringing certain products to market. &nbsp;Litigation concerning patents and proprietary rights is often protracted and expensive. &nbsp;Pharmaceutical companies with patented brand products increasingly are suing companies that produce generic forms of their products for alleged patent infringement or other violations of intellectual property rights, which could delay or prevent the entry of such generic products into the market. &nbsp;Generally, a generic drug may not be marketed until the applicable patent(s) on the brand drug expires. &nbsp;When an ANDA is filed with the FDA for approval of a generic drug, the filer may certify either that any patent listed by the FDA as covering the brand product is about to expire, in which case the ANDA will not become effective until the expiration of such patent, or that the patent listed as covering the brand drug is invalid or will not be infringed by the manufacture, sale or use of the new drug for which the ANDA is filed. &nbsp;In either case, there is a risk that a brand pharmaceutical company may sue the filer for alleged patent infringement or other violations of intellectual property rights. &nbsp;Because a substantial portion of our current business involves the marketing and development of generic versions of brand products, the threat of litigation, the outcome of which is inherently uncertain, is always present. &nbsp;Such litigation is often costly and time-consuming, and could result in a substantial delay in, or prevent, the introduction and/or marketing of products, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, prospects and results of operations. &nbsp;</p> <p metoprolol succinate ER. &nbsp;The dollar amount decrease of metoprolol revenues for 2011 can be attributed to a decrease in the volume of units sold (approximately 51% of total dollar decrease for 2011) with the remainder of the dollar amount decrease due to price. &nbsp;We expect metoprolol revenues to continue to decline in the future as competition increases in this market. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; FONT-SIZE:1pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-1pt" /> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p voluntarily withdrawn from the distribution channel. &nbsp;Because of these events, Par has discontinued marketing clonidine. </p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; 2010 and additional competition for sumatriptan beginning in the third quarter of 2011. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; competition from its authorized generic. </p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px" align=center>41</p> <p decreases above were tempered by; </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; chlorpheniramine/hydrocodone in October 2010. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Improved 2011 royalties primarily from the sales of diazepam, which launched in September 2010, and from the sales of fenofibrate, both of which are included in Par Pharmaceutical as &#147;Other product related revenues&#148;. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Net sales of contract-manufactured products (which are manufactured for us by third parties under contract) and licensed products (which are licensed to us from third-party development partners and also are generally manufactured by third parties) were approximately 58% of our total product revenues for 2011 and approximately 71% of our total product revenues for 2010. &nbsp;The decrease in the percentage is primarily driven by decreased revenues of metoprolol and clonidine combined with the launches of propafenone, and amlodipine and benazepril HCl. &nbsp;We are substantially dependent upon contract-manufactured and licensed products for our overall sales, and any inability by our suppliers to meet demand could adversely affect our future sales. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">The decrease in the Strativa segment revenues in 2011 was primarily due to the decrease in other product-related revenues, driven by the termination of an agreement to co-promote Androgel<sup>&#174;</sup> in December 2010 coupled with a net sales decline of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES primarily due to decreased volume coupled with a decrease in average net selling price as compared to 2010. &nbsp;The decreases were tempered by the continued growth of Nascobal<sup>&#174; </sup>in 2011 and the latter half of 2010 launches of Oravig<sup>&#174; </sup>and Zuplenz<sup>&#174; </sup>and milestone payments earned in 2011 pertaining to an agreement with Optimer related to fidaxomicin. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px; LINE-HEIGHT:12pt">Strativa launched Oravig<sup>&#174; </sup>in the third quarter of 2010 and Zuplenz<sup>&#174;</sup> in the fourth quarter of 2010. &nbsp;In connection with the launches, our direct customers ordered, and we shipped, Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> and Zuplenz<sup>&#174; </sup>units at a level commensurate with initial forecasted demand for the products. &nbsp;Due to our relatively limited history in the branded pharmaceutical marketplace, it is impractical to predict with reasonable certainty the rate of Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup>&#146;s and Zuplenz<sup>&#174;</sup>&#146;s<sup> </sup>prescription demand uptake and ultimate acceptance in the marketplace. &nbsp;Therefore, we recognize revenue and all associated cost of sales as the product is prescribed to patients based on an analysis of third party market prescription data, third party wholesaler inventory data, order refill rates, and all substantive quantitative and qualitative data available to us at the time for Oravig<sup>&#174; </sup>and Zuplenz<sup>&#174;</sup>. &nbsp;Accordingly, for 2011, we have recognized $2.4 million of Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> revenues and $0.9 million of Zuplenz<sup>&#174; </sup>revenues and deferred revenues of $0.2 million for Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> and of $0.4 million for Zuplenz<sup>&#174;</sup>, related to product that has been shipped to customers but not yet been prescribed to patients. &nbsp;In June 2011, we resized our Strativa business. &nbsp;As part of this strategic assessment, we reduced our Strativa workforce by approximately 90 people. &nbsp;Refer to Note 20 &#150; &#147;Restructuring Costs.&#148; &nbsp;We will continue to recognize revenue and all associated cost of sales as Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> and Zuplenz<font style="FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman"><b><sup>&#174;</sup></b></font> are prescribed to patients based on an analysis of third party market prescription data, third party wholesaler inventory data, order refill rates, and all substantive quantitative and qualitative data available to us. &nbsp;In July 2011, Strativa returned the U.S. commercialization rights of Zuplenz<sup>&#174; </sup>to MonoSol, as part of the resizing of Strativa. &nbsp;In September 2011, Strativa executed a termination agreement with BioAlliance returning all Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> rights and obligations to BioAlliance. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:13px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px" were no longer the sole generic distributor. &nbsp;Our sales and related gross margins for clonidine TDS were negatively impacted. &nbsp;</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; tramadol ER, both of which are manufactured by Par and both of which launched in the fourth quarter of 2009, combined with decreased revenues of metoprolol and clonidine. &nbsp;We are substantially prescription levels, tempered by a single digit increase in average net selling price. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px" align=justify>&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px" align=center>43</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px" align=justify> <hr> <p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px" align=justify><br></p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:36px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-24px"><i>Gross Revenues to Total Revenues Deductions</i></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Generic drug pricing at the wholesale level can create significant differences between our invoice price and net selling price. &nbsp;Wholesale customers purchase product from us at invoice price, then resell the product to specific healthcare providers on the basis of prices negotiated between us and the providers, and the wholesaler submits a chargeback credit to us for the difference. &nbsp;We record estimates for these chargebacks as well as sales returns, rebates and incentive programs, and the sales allowances for all our customers at the time of sale as deductions from gross revenues, with corresponding adjustments to our accounts receivable reserves and allowances.<b> </b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">We have the experience and the access to relevant information that we believe necessary to reasonably estimate the amounts of such deductions from gross revenues. &nbsp;Some of the assumptions we use for certain of our estimates are based on information received from third parties, such as wholesale customer inventory data and market data, or other market factors beyond our control. &nbsp;The estimates that are most critical to the establishment of these reserves, and therefore would have the largest impact if these estimates were not accurate, are estimates related to expected contract sales volumes, average contract pricing, customer inventories and return levels. &nbsp;We regularly review the information related to these estimates and adjust our reserves accordingly if and when actual experience differs from previous estimates. &nbsp;With the exception of the product returns allowance, the ending balances of account receivable reserves and allowances generally are eliminated during a two-month to four-month period, on average.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px; LINE-HEIGHT:12pt">We recognize revenue for product sales when title and risk of loss have transferred to our customers and when collectability is reasonably assured. &nbsp;This is generally at the time that products are received by the customers. &nbsp;Upon recognizing revenue from a sale, we record estimates for chargebacks, rebates and incentives, returns, cash discounts and other sales reserves that reduce accounts receivable. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Our gross revenues for the years ended December 31, 2011, December 31, 2010 and December 31, 2009 before deductions for chargebacks, rebates and incentive programs (including rebates style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The total gross-to-net adjustments as a percentage of sales increased for 2011 compared to 2010 primarily due to an increase in medicaid rebates and rebates due under other U.S. Government pricing programs, chargebacks, and cash discounts and other.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Chargebacks: the increase in the percentage of gross revenues was primarily driven by higher chargeback rates for certain products that had limited or no competition in the comparable period in 2010 and 2009. </p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Rebates and incentive programs: the slight decrease in dollars was primarily driven by product mix, mainly metoprolol and clonidine, partially offset by the impact of new product launches.</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Returns:&nbsp;the increase in the rate was driven by higher returns experienced for sumatriptan, clonidine and dronabinol, partially offset by increased sales volume of products with lower than average return rates.&nbsp; </p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:3px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Cash discounts and other: the increase is primarily due to a change in customer mix, mainly for metoprolol, which resulted in higher price adjustments.</p> <p style="CLEAR:left; MARGIN-TOP:0px; FLOAT:left; MARGIN-BOTTOM:-2px; WIDTH:48px; TEXT-INDENT:24px; FONT-FAMILY:Symbol">&#183;</p> <p style="PADDING-LEFT:48px; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:-2px">Medicaid rebates and rebates due under other U.S. Government pricing programs: expense increase was due to the full year-to-date period impact of the March 2010 health care reform acts, which led to higher Medicaid rebate rates and additional patients eligible for managed Medicaid benefits, coupled with the Medicare Part D - Gap Coverage, which was effective in the first quarter of 2011.&nbsp; </p> <p December 2010 coupled with a net sales decline of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES, primarily due to decreased volume tempered by higher revenues from Nascobal<sup>&#174;</sup>. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">For 2011, the impact of healthcare reform resulted in a decrease of approximately $7.3 million to our total gross margin. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p> litigation tempered by cash generated from operations. &nbsp;The working capital ratio, which is calculated by dividing current assets by current liabilities, was 2.08x at December 31, 2011 compared MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px"><i>Sources of Liquidity</i></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Our primary source of liquidity is cash received from customers. &nbsp;In 2010, we collected approximately $1,098 million with respect to net product sales as compared to approximately $941 million in 2011. &nbsp;The decrease for 2011 as compared to the prior year can be attributed to lower cash receipts from customers, as detailed above, driven primarily by lower sales of metoprolol and clonidine tempered by the launches of budesonide and propafenone. &nbsp;Our ability to continue to generate cash from operations is predicated not only on our ability to maintain a sustainable amount of sales of our current product portfolio, but also our ability to monetize our product pipeline and future products that we may acquire. &nbsp;Our Par generic product pipeline consisted of approximately 72 ANDAs pending with the FDA, including 19 first-to-file and four first-to-market opportunities as of December 31, 2011. &nbsp;Our future profitability depends, to a significant extent, upon our ability to introduce, on a timely basis, new generic products that are either the first-to-market (or among the first-to-market) or otherwise can gain significant market share. &nbsp;No assurances can be given that we or any of our strategic partners will successfully complete the development of any of these potential products either under development or proposed for development, that regulatory approvals will be granted for any such product, that any approved product will be produced in commercial quantities or that any approved product will be sold profitably. &nbsp;Commercializing brand pharmaceutical products is more costly than generic products. &nbsp;We cannot be certain that our brand product expenditures will result in the successful development or launch of brand products that will prove to be commercially successful or will improve the long-term profitability of our business. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:3px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Another source of potential liquidity is the capital markets. &nbsp;We filed a &#147;shelf&#148; registration statement during the second quarter of 2009, under which we may sell a combination of common stock, preferred stock, debt securities, or warrants from time to time for an aggregate offering price of up to $150 million. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:2px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">On November 17, 2011 we entered into a credit agreement with a syndicate of banks, led by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as Administrative Agent, U.S. Bank National Association and PNC Bank National Association as Co-Syndication Agents, DnB NOR Bank ASA and SunTrust Bank as Co-Documentation Agents and J.P. Morgan Securities LLC as Sole Bookrunner and Lead Arranger, to provide senior unsecured credit facilities comprised of a five-year Term Loan Facility in an initial aggregate principal amount of $350 million and a five-year Revolving Credit Facility in an initial amount of $100 million. &nbsp;We used the proceeds of the Term Loan Facility, together with cash on hand, to finance the Anchen Acquisition, and the proceeds of the Revolving Credit Facility are available for general corporate purposes. &nbsp;The credit agreement includes an expansion feature pursuant to which we can increase the amount available to be borrowed by up to an additional $150 million under certain circumstances. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, there was $346 million outstanding under the Term Loan Facility while no amounts were outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:2px;
