align=center>F-32</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px>&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px> <hr> <br> <p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><i>Chief Executive Officer Specific Share-based Compensation</i></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">On November&nbsp;2, 2010, we entered into a new employment agreement with Patrick LePore, in his capacity as President and Chief Executive Officer, effective as of January&nbsp;1, 2011. &nbsp;His new employment agreement is for a three-year term, ending December&nbsp;31, 2013, subject to certain early termination events. &nbsp;Pursuant to the employment agreement, Mr. LePore is eligible to receive an incentive compensation award based on the compound annual growth rate (&#147;CAGR&#148;) of our common stock over the course of Mr. LePore&#146;s three-year employment term (January 1, 2011 to December 31, 2013). &nbsp;Mr. LePore will be eligible to receive an incentive compensation award ranging from $2&nbsp;million (for a three-year CAGR of 4%) to $9&nbsp;million (for a three-year CAGR of 20% or more). &nbsp;He will not be eligible to receive an incentive compensation award if the Company&#146;s three-year CAGR is below 4%, and no incentive compensation award will be payable if the employment agreement is terminated prior to its expiration unless a change of control (as defined in the agreement) has occurred. &nbsp;These CAGR based awards will be classified as liability awards and are reported within accrued expenses and other current liabilities and other long-term liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet. &nbsp;The fair values of these awards are remeasured at each reporting period (mark-to-market) using a Monte Carlo valuation model until the awards vest and are paid. &nbsp;Fair value fluctuations are recognized as cumulative adjustments to share-based compensation expense and the related liabilities. &nbsp;Share-based compensation expense for these CAGR awards will be recognized ratably over the three-year service period. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our CAGR was below 4% from January 1, 2011. &nbsp;Through December 31, 2011, we recognized $362 thousand of expense associated with this plan.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In January 2011, Mr. LePore was granted an equity award consisting of restricted stock units with a total grant date economic value of approximately $1.85 million. &nbsp;The units will vest on the earlier of (a)&nbsp;the expiration of Mr. LePore&#146;s employment term on December 31, 2013, (b)&nbsp;the date that a change of control (as defined in the agreement) occurs, or (c)&nbsp;the date of an eligible earlier termination of Mr. LePore&#146;s employment term in accordance with the provisions of the agreement. &nbsp;The related share-based compensation expense is being recorded over the three-year term of the new employment agreement, which is the vesting period. &nbsp;The fair value of restricted stock units was based on the market value of our common stock on the date of grant.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>Note Options granted under the 1997 Directors&#146; Plan become exercisable in full on the first anniversary of the date of grant, so long as the eligible director has not been removed &#147;for cause&#148; as a member of the Board on or prior to the first anniversary of the date of grant. The maximum term of an option under the 1997 Directors&#146; Plan is ten years. &nbsp;Prior to the 2007 amendment and restatement, the 1997 Directors&#146; Plan also provided for the granting of restricted stock units that vest over 4 years. &nbsp;Upon the amendment and restatement of the 1997 Directors&#146; Plan approved by the stockholders in 2007, non-employee directors, effective January 1, 2008, receive an annual grant of restricted stock units equal to the fair market value of $100,000, which vest one year from the anniversary of the date of grant unless the director has been removed &#147;for cause.&#148; &nbsp;The restricted stock units are not issued or otherwise distributed to the director until the director terminates service on the Board. &nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, Par has reserved 142 shares of common stock for issuance under the 1997 Directors&#146; Plan. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px>&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px>&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px>&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>F-34</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px> <hr> <p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Under all of our stock option plans, the stock option exercise price of all the options granted equaled the market price on the date of grant. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">In October 2004, the Board adopted a stockholder rights plan designed to ensure that all of our stockholders receive fair and equal treatment in the event of an unsolicited attempt to acquire us. &nbsp;The adoption of the rights plan is intended to deter partial and &#147;two step&#148; tender offers or other coercive takeover tactics, and to prevent an acquirer from gaining control of us without offering a fair price to all of our stockholders. &nbsp;The rights plan was not adopted in response to any known offers for us and is similar to stockholder rights plans adopted by many other public companies. </p> <p style="FONT-SIZE:8pt; MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">To implement the rights plan, the Board declared a distribution of one preferred stock purchase right per share of common stock, payable to all stockholders of record as of November 8, 2004. &nbsp;The rights will be distributed as a non-taxable dividend and expire on October 27, 2014. &nbsp;The rights will be evidenced by the underlying Company common stock, and no separate preferred stock purchase rights certificates will presently be distributed. &nbsp;The rights to acquire preferred stock are not immediately exercisable and will become exercisable only if a person or group acquires or commences a tender offer for 15% or more of our common stock.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">If a person or group acquires or commences a tender offer for 15% or more of our common stock, each holder of a right, except the acquirer, will be entitled, subject to our right to redeem or exchange the right, to exercise, at an exercise price of $225, the right for one one-thousandth of a share of our newly-created Series A Junior Participating Preferred Stock, or the number of shares of our common stock equal to the holder&#146;s number of rights multiplied by the exercise price and divided by 50% of the market price of our common stock on the date of the occurrence of such an event. &nbsp;The Board may terminate the rights plan at any time or redeem the rights, for $0.01 per right, at any time before a person or group acquires 15% or more of Par&#146;s common stock.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><b>Note 16 </b><font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><b>-</font> Income Taxes:</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><i>Tax Contingencies</i></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Significant judgment is required in evaluating our tax positions and determining its provision for income taxes. &nbsp;During the ordinary course of business, there are many transactions and calculations for which the ultimate tax determination is uncertain. &nbsp;We establish reserves for tax-related uncertainties based on estimates of whether, and the extent to which, additional taxes will be due. &nbsp;These reserves are established when we believe that certain positions might be challenged despite our belief that our tax return positions are fully supportable. &nbsp;We adjust these reserves in light of changing facts and circumstances, such as the outcome of tax audits. &nbsp;The provision for income taxes includes the impact of reserve provisions and changes to reserves that are considered appropriate. &nbsp;Accruals for tax contingencies are provided for in accordance with the requirements of ASC 740-10. &nbsp;We reflect interest and penalties attributable to income taxes, to the extent they arise, as a component of its income tax provision or benefit.&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px" align=center>F-36</p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px"> <hr> <p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">At December 31, 2011, the total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits (excluding the federal benefit received from state positions) was $14.4&nbsp;million. &nbsp;Of this total, $9.8&nbsp;million (net of the federal benefit on state issues) represents the amount of unrecognized tax benefits that, if recognized, would favorably affect the effective tax rate related to continuing income in future periods. &nbsp;The total amount of accrued interest and penalties resulting from such unrecognized tax benefits was $5.8 million at December 31, 2011 and $11.3 million at December 31, 2010. &nbsp;During the years ended December 31, 2011, 2010, and 2009, we recognized approximately $0.4 million, $0.6 million, and $0.7 million in interest and penalties.</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">We have a Retirement Savings Plan (the &#147;Retirement Savings Plan&#148;) whereby eligible employees are permitted to contribute annually from 1% to 25% of their compensation to the Retirement Savings Plan. &nbsp;We contribute an amount equal to 50% of up to the first 6% of compensation contributed by the employee (&#147;401(k) matching feature&#148;). &nbsp;Participants in the Retirement Savings Plan become vested with respect to 20% of our contributions for each full year of employment with the Company and thus become fully vested after five full years. &nbsp;We also may contribute additional funds each year to the Retirement Savings Plan, the amount of which, if any, is determined by the Board in its sole discretion. &nbsp;We incurred expenses related to the 401(k) matching feature of the Retirement Savings Plan of $1.2 million in 2011, $1.2 million in 2010, and $1.4 million in 2009. &nbsp;We did not make a discretionary contribution to the Retirement Savings Plan for 2011, 2010 or 2009.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Par&#146;s Anchen subsidiary has a legacy 401(k) plan whereby its eligible employees are permitted to contribute annually from their compensation to this 401(k) plan up to the annual IRS limit. &nbsp;Under this plan, Anchen eligible employees can receive employer matching contributions of 100% of the first 3% of compensation contributed and 50% of the next 2% of compensation contributed (&#147;Anchen 401(k) matching feature&#148;). &nbsp;Participants in the legacy 401(k) plan become vested immediately with respect to the Anchen 401(k) matching feature contributions each pay period. &nbsp;Anchen eligible employees may also receive additional funds each year under the legacy 401(k) plan, the amount of which, if any, is determined by the Board in its sole discretion. &nbsp;We incurred expenses related to the Anchen 401(k) matching feature of $50 thousand in 2011. &nbsp;We did not make a discretionary contribution to the legacy 401(k) plan for 2011. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify>&nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify>&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify>&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=center>F-37</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px align=justify> <hr> <p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px"><b>Industry Related Matters &nbsp;</b></p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px">Beginning in September 2003, we, along with numerous other pharmaceutical companies, have been named as a defendant in actions brought by a number of state Attorneys General and municipal bodies within the state of New York, as well as a federal <i>qui tam </i>action brought on behalf of the United States by the pharmacy Ven-A-Care of the Florida Keys, Inc. ("Ven-A-Care") alleging generally that the defendants defrauded the state Medicaid systems by purportedly reporting &#147;Average Wholesale Prices&#148; (&#147;AWP&#148;) and/or &#147;Wholesale Acquisition Costs&#148; that exceeded the actual selling price of the defendants&#146; prescription drugs.&nbsp; To date, we have been named as a defendant in substantially similar civil law suits filed by the Attorneys General of Alabama, Alaska, Florida, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Texas, Utah and Wisconsin, and also by the city of New York, 46 counties across New York State and Ven-A-Care.&nbsp; These cases generally seek some combination of actual damages, and/or double damages, treble damages, compensatory damages, statutory damages, civil penalties, disgorgement of excessive profits, restitution, disbursements, counsel fees and costs, litigation expenses, investigative costs, injunctive relief, punitive damages, imposition of a constructive trust, accounting of profits or gains derived through the alleged conduct, expert fees, interest and other relief that the court deems proper.&nbsp; In the Utah suit, the time for responding to the complaint has not yet elapsed. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Hawaii suit was settled on August 25, 2010 for $2,250 thousand. &nbsp;&nbsp;The Massachusetts suit was settled on December 17, 2010 for $500 thousand. &nbsp;The Alabama suit was settled on January 5, 2011 for $2,500 thousand. &nbsp;The Idaho suit was settled on March 25, 2011 for $1,700 thousand. &nbsp;On August 24, 2011, we settled claims brought by Ven-A-Care, Texas, and Florida, under federal and state law, as well as Alaska, South Carolina, and Kentucky under state law, for $154,000 thousand. &nbsp;The settlement resolved the lawsuit relating to federal contributions to state Medicaid programs in 49 states (excluding Illinois), and claims of Texas, Florida, Alaska, South Carolina and Kentucky relating to their Medicaid programs. The settlement eliminated the majority of the alleged damages asserted against us in the various drug pricing litigations and removed all trials that had been scheduled. &nbsp;We paid the $154,000 thousand settlement amount during the third quarter of 2011. &nbsp;On June 2, 2011, we reached a settlement in principle to resolve claims brought by the city of New York, New York Counties and the state of Iowa under respective state law for $23,000 thousand. &nbsp;The Mississippi suit was settled on September 1, 2011 for $3,600 thousand. &nbsp;On October 18, 2011, we reached an agreement in principle to settle the Oklahoma suit for $884 thousand. &nbsp;The remaining matters have yet to be scheduled for trial. &nbsp;We have accrued a $37,800 thousand reserve under the caption &#147;Accrued legal settlements&#148; on our consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2011, in connection with the June 2, 2011 settlement in principle and the remaining AWP actions. &nbsp;In each of the remaining matters, we have either moved to dismiss the complaints or answered the complaints denying liability.&nbsp; We will continue to defend or explore settlement opportunities in other jurisdictions as we feel are in our best interest under the circumstances presented in those jurisdictions. &nbsp;However, we can give no assurance that we will be able to settle the remaining actions on terms that we deem reasonable, or that such settlements or adverse judgments, if entered, will not exceed the amount of the reserve.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">The Attorneys General of Florida, Indiana and Virginia and the United States Office of Personnel Management (the &#147;USOPM&#148;) have issued subpoenas, and the Attorneys General of Michigan, Tennessee, Texas, and Utah have issued civil investigative demands, to us.&nbsp; The demands generally request documents and information pertaining to allegations that certain of our sales and marketing practices caused pharmacies to substitute ranitidine capsules for ranitidine tablets, fluoxetine tablets for fluoxetine capsules, and two 7.5 mg buspirone tablets for one 15 mg buspirone tablet, under circumstances in which some state Medicaid programs at various times reimbursed the new dosage form at a higher rate than the dosage form being substituted.&nbsp; We have provided documents in response to these subpoenas to the respective Attorneys General and the USOPM. &nbsp;The aforementioned subpoenas and civil investigative demands culminated in the federal and state law <i>qui tam</i> action brought on behalf of the United States and several states by Bernard Lisitza. &nbsp;The complaint was unsealed on August 30, 2011. &nbsp;The United States intervened in this action on July 8, 2011 and filed a separate complaint on September 9, 2011, alleging claims for violations of the Federal False Claims Act and common law fraud. &nbsp;We intend to vigorously defend this lawsuit. &nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">We have also been named a defendant in a putative federal class action brought by the United Food and Commercial Workers Unions and Employers Midwest Health Benefits Fund (&#147;UFCW&#148;) under the Federal Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act alleging the same general conduct as set forth in the preceding paragraph. &nbsp;The time for responding to the complaint filed by UFCW has not yet elapsed. &nbsp;We intend to vigorously defend this lawsuit.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px"><b>Department of Justice Matter</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">On March 19, 2009, we were served with a subpoena by the Department of Justice requesting documents related to Strativa&#146;s marketing of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES.&nbsp; The subpoena indicated that the Department of Justice is currently investigating promotional practices in the sales and marketing of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES.&nbsp; We believe that our marketing of Megace<sup>&#174;</sup> ES has complied with all applicable laws and we have provided, or are in the process of providing, documents in response to this subpoena to the Department of Justice and will continue to cooperate with the Department of Justice in this inquiry if called upon to do so. &nbsp;Investigations of this type often result in settlements, including&nbsp;monetary amounts based on an agreed upon percentage of sales of the product at issue in the investigation. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:13px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">&nbsp;</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:0px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:6px; TEXT-INDENT:48px; FONT-FAMILY:Times New Roman Bold,Times New Roman"><b>Other</b></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">We are, from time to time, a party to certain other litigations, including product liability litigations. &nbsp;We believe that these litigations are part of the ordinary course of our business and that their ultimate resolution will not have a material effect on our financial condition, results of operations or liquidity. We intend to defend or, in cases where we are the plaintiff, to prosecute these litigations vigorously.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:20px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px"><b>Note 18 </b><font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><b>-</font> Discontinued Operations &#150; Related Party Transaction: </b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In January 2006, we divested FineTech Laboratories, Ltd (&#147;FineTech&#148;), effective December 31, 2005. &nbsp;We transferred the business for no proceeds to Dr. Arie Gutman, president and chief executive officer of FineTech. &nbsp;Dr. Gutman also resigned from our Board of Directors. &nbsp;In 2011, 2010 and 2009 we recorded tax amounts to discontinued operations for interest related to contingent tax liabilities. &nbsp;In addition, in 2010, we recognized a tax benefit of approximately $400 thousand to discontinued operations due to the resolution of certain tax contingencies. &nbsp;In 2011, we recognized a tax benefit of approximately $20,000 thousand to discontinued operations due to a reversal of certain FineTech related contingent tax liabilities. &nbsp;The results of FineTech operations are classified as discontinued for all periods presented because we have no continuing involvement in FineTech. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><b>Note 19 </b><font style=FONT-FAMILY:Symbol><b>-</font> Segment Information:</b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">We operate in two reportable business segments: generic pharmaceuticals (referred to as &#147;Par Pharmaceutical&#148; or &#147;Par&#148;) and branded pharmaceuticals (referred to as &#147;Strativa Pharmaceuticals&#148; or &#147;Strativa&#148;). &nbsp;Branded products are marketed under brand names through marketing programs that are designed to generate physician and consumer loyalty. &nbsp;Branded products generally are patent protected, which provides a period of market exclusivity during which they are sold with little or no direct competition. &nbsp;Generic pharmaceutical products are the chemical and therapeutic equivalents of corresponding brand drugs. &nbsp;The Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act of 1984 provides that generic drugs may enter the market upon the approval of an ANDA and the expiration, invalidation or circumvention of any patents on corresponding brand drugs, or the expiration of any other market exclusivity periods related to the brand drugs. Our chief operating decision maker is our Chief Executive Officer. &nbsp;&nbsp;</p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">Our business segments were determined based on management&#146;s reporting and decision-making requirements in accordance with FASB ASC 280-10 Segment Reporting. &nbsp;We believe that our generic products represent a single operating segment because the demand for these products is mainly driven by consumers seeking a lower cost alternative to brand name drugs. &nbsp;Par&#146;s generic drugs are developed using similar methodologies, for the same purpose (e.g., seeking bioequivalence with a brand name drug nearing the end of its market exclusivity period for any reason discussed above). &nbsp;Par&#146;s generic products are produced using similar processes and standards mandated by the FDA, and Par&#146;s generic products are sold to similar customers. &nbsp;Based on the economic characteristics, production processes and customers of Par&#146;s generic products, management has determined that Par&#146;s generic pharmaceuticals are a single reportable business segment. &nbsp;Our chief operating decision maker does not review the Par (generic) or Strativa (brand) segments in any more granularity, such as at the therapeutic or other classes or categories. &nbsp;Certain of our expenses, such as the direct sales force and other sales and marketing expenses and specific research and development expenses, are charged directly to either of the two segments. &nbsp;&nbsp;Other expenses, such as general and administrative expenses and non-specific research and development expenses are allocated between the two segments based on assumptions determined by management. </p> <p style=MARGIN:0px>&nbsp;</p> <p Costs: </b></p> <p style=MARGIN:0px><br></p> <p style="MARGIN:0px; TEXT-INDENT:36px; LINE-HEIGHT:12pt">In 2008, we announced our plans to resize Par Pharmaceutical, our generic products division, as part of an ongoing strategic assessment of our businesses. &nbsp;These actions resulted in a workforce reduction of approximately 190 positions in manufacturing, research and development, and general and administrative functions. &nbsp;In connection with these actions, we incurred expenses for severance and other employee-related costs. &nbsp;In addition, we made the determination to abandon or sell certain assets that resulted in asset impairments, and accelerated depreciation expense. &nbsp;During the year ended 2009, we incurred additional restructuring costs as we continued to execute this plan, principally driven by charges for one-time termination benefit costs recognized. &nbsp;These charges were somewhat tempered by a modest revision in estimate of certain termination benefit costs. </p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">In June 2011, we announced our plans to resize Strativa Pharmaceuticals, our branded products division, as part of a strategic assessment. &nbsp;We reduced our Strativa workforce by approximately 90 people. &nbsp;The remaining Strativa sales force focus their marketing efforts on Megace<sup>&#174; </sup>ES and Nascobal<sup>&#174; </sup>Nasal Spray. &nbsp;In connection with these actions, we incurred expenses for severance and other employee-related costs. &nbsp;The intangible assets related to products no longer a priority for our remaining Strativa sales force were fully impaired by these actions. &nbsp;We also had non-cash inventory write downs for product and samples associated with the products no longer a priority for our remaining Strativa sales force. &nbsp;Inventory write downs were classified as cost of goods sold on the consolidated statements of operations for the year ended December 31, 2011. &nbsp;In July 2011, Strativa returned the U.S. commercialization rights of Zuplenz<sup>&#174; </sup>to MonoSol, as part of the resizing of Strativa. &nbsp;In September 2011, Strativa executed a termination agreement with BioAlliance returning all Oravig<sup>&#174;</sup> rights and obligations to BioAlliance.</p> <p style="MARGIN-TOP:6px; MARGIN-BOTTOM:0px; TEXT-INDENT:48px">&nbsp;</p> <p
